A client receiving a blood transfusion and two clients on continuous cardiac monitoring
Four stable clients awaiting discharge teaching and routine postoperative care
items.rationale: A floated nurse is assigned clients whose care falls within skills common to all registered nurses, and the charge nurse keeps the clients requiring unit-specific competencies. Stable clients needing routine care and discharge teaching fit that rule. Transfusion monitoring, telemetry, chest tube management and titrated vasopressors require competencies a postpartum nurse is unlikely to have validated, so assigning them shifts risk onto the client.

items.stem: A client being discharged with asthma has a prescription for a brand-name inhaler that the client's insurance plan does not cover, and the client states the cash price is unaffordable. Which action by the nurse is most appropriate?
options: Suggest the client borrow a relative's inhaler until the prescription can be filled
Advise the client to pay out of pocket this month and reassess at the follow-up visit
Give the client sample inhalers from the clinic supply to last a month
Contact the pharmacist and prescriber about a therapeutically equivalent inhaler on the client's formulary
items.rationale: Cost-effective care means securing the same therapeutic effect through a medication the client can actually obtain and refill, and the pharmacist is the team member who identifies formulary alternatives for the prescriber to approve. Samples bridge a few weeks and then leave the client with the same unaffordable prescription. Advising unaffordable out-of-pocket payment predicts nonadherence, and sharing another person's prescription medication is never acceptable.

items.stem: A nurse realizes that a completed physical assessment was documented in the wrong client's electronic health record. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Ask the unit secretary to remove the note from the chart
Write an explanatory note at the end of the shift describing what happened
Delete the entry so that the record contains only accurate information
Mark the entry as an error according to facility policy, document in the correct record, and notify health information management
items.rationale: Electronic records are permanent: an incorrect entry is marked as an error with the reason, the correct documentation is entered in the right chart, and health information management is notified so the wrong record is amended and any release of that information is tracked. Deleting an entry, or having another person alter it, destroys the audit trail and may be viewed as falsification. Waiting until the end of the shift leaves another clinician acting on a record that describes the wrong person.

items.stem: A nurse is preparing to draw blood for a type and crossmatch on a hospitalized client. Which pair of identifiers meets the requirement to use two client identifiers?
options: The client's full name and date of birth
The client's room number and bed letter
The client's diagnosis and attending provider's name
The client's full name and room number
items.rationale: Acceptable identifiers are specific to the person and travel with the client, such as the full name, date of birth or medical record number, verified against the wristband and stated by the client whenever possible. Room and bed assignments belong to a location and change whenever the client is moved, which is exactly how wrong-client specimens occur. A diagnosis or a provider's name is shared by many clients and identifies no one.

items.stem: A unit team using the plan-do-study-act model has collected 4 weeks of baseline data showing that 38% of medications are given without barcode scanning. Which step should the team take next?
options: Report the nurses with the lowest scanning rates to the nurse manager
Collect another 4 weeks of baseline data to confirm the finding
Test one change, such as placing a working scanner at every bedside, on a single hall for 2 weeks
Write a policy requiring 100% scanning and distribute it to all staff
items.rationale: After the plan phase establishes a baseline, the do phase is a small, rapid test of one change in a limited setting, so its effect can be studied before it is spread. Small tests reveal why the workaround exists, which broad policy statements never do. Naming individuals treats a system problem as a discipline problem and suppresses reporting, and repeating baseline measurement gathers more data without changing anything.

items.stem: A client with metastatic lung cancer is continuing chemotherapy and reports uncontrolled pain, nausea and fatigue that are interfering with daily life. The client asks the nurse, 'Is there anyone who can help me with these symptoms?' Which referral is most appropriate?
options: Hospice services, which provide comprehensive symptom management at home
A home health aide to assist with activities of daily living
Chaplain services for support in coping with the diagnosis
Palliative care, which can be provided alongside disease-directed treatment
items.rationale: Palliative care is specialized symptom and goals-of-care support that is offered at any stage of a serious illness and runs concurrently with curative or disease-directed therapy. Hospice serves clients who are no longer pursuing disease-directed treatment and generally have a prognosis of 6 months or less, so it does not fit a client continuing chemotherapy. A home aide assists with self-care, and chaplaincy addresses spiritual distress, neither of which manages pain and nausea.

items.stem: A new graduate nurse asks what the hospital case manager contributes to the interdisciplinary team. Which responsibilities belong to the case manager? Select all that apply.
options: Screening clients for readmission risk and arranging follow-up appointments
Performing the client's daily head-to-toe assessment
Coordinating insurance authorization for post-acute placement
Prescribing the client's discharge medications
Facilitating family meetings about the discharge plan
Arranging home health services and durable medical equipment
items.rationale: Case managers own the movement of the client through and out of the system: authorizations, post-acute placement, home services and equipment, readmission risk screening and the family conferences where the plan is agreed on. Daily physical assessment remains the bedside nurse's responsibility, and prescribing is within the provider's scope. Knowing where each role begins prevents both duplicated effort and gaps that surface only after the client is home.

items.stem: A nurse is preparing to conduct a scheduled video visit with a client at home. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
options: Conduct the visit from a private area and confirm that the client can also speak privately
Verify the client's identity with two identifiers at the start of the visit
Assume the client has consented to the virtual visit by joining the call
Confirm the client's physical location in case emergency services are needed
Record the visit on a personal phone in order to chart from it later
Document the encounter in the record as a telehealth visit, including the platform used
items.rationale: A virtual visit carries the same identification, privacy, consent and documentation requirements as an in-person encounter, with one addition: the nurse confirms where the client physically is, because that is where emergency services would be sent. Consent to telehealth is obtained and documented rather than inferred from the client's presence on the call. Recording a clinical encounter on a personal device removes protected information from the secure system and violates privacy rules.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client who had a transtibial amputation 2 weeks ago is preparing to go home to a single-story house with three steps at the only entrance. The nurse should arrange a referral to {{1}}. The durable medical equipment most likely to be needed at discharge is {{2}}.

options: physical therapy for prosthetic training and transfer practice
the infection preventionist
respiratory therapy
speech-language pathology
an oxygen concentrator with portable tanks
a continuous passive motion machine
a mechanical lift with a sling
a wheelchair with an evaluation for a ramp at the entrance

items.rationale: Prosthetic gait training, transfers and residual limb care belong to physical therapy, and the entry steps mean the client needs both wheeled mobility and a way through the door, which is why a ramp evaluation accompanies the wheelchair order. Equipment that does not match the deficit adds cost without improving safety. Identifying access barriers before discharge, rather than after the first failed attempt, keeps the client out of the emergency department.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: At the end of the shift the nurse finds that the 0900 dose of metoprolol is documented as given, but the tablet is still in the client's medication drawer. The nurse should first {{1}}. The event should then be {{2}}.

options: ask the oncoming nurse to follow up on the missed dose
correct the entry to show the dose was not given and continue the shift
assess the client, obtain the heart rate and blood pressure, and notify the prescriber
give the tablet now and leave the original entry unchanged
handled informally between the nurses involved
reported to the state board of nursing
documented in the client's chart as an incident report
reported through the facility's occurrence reporting system

items.rationale: A missed dose is first a clinical question: the current heart rate and blood pressure determine whether the beta blocker can still be given safely or whether the prescriber must adjust the plan, so assessment precedes correcting the record. The documentation is then corrected as a charting error, and the event goes into the occurrence reporting system so the cause, such as documenting before administering, is examined. Occurrence reports are never filed in the chart.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the home visit note that require referral to another member of the interdisciplinary team.

highlightSegments.text: 1030 Routine home visit for an 84-year-old client with heart failure and osteoarthritis.
Blood pressure 128/74 mm Hg and weight unchanged from the previous week.
Client has fallen twice in the past month while stepping over the side of the bathtub.
Client states, 'I cannot open my pill bottles anymore because of my hands.'
Medications are taken from a weekly organizer that a neighbor fills each Sunday.
Client states, 'I mostly eat canned soup and lunch meat because cooking tires me out.'
Lungs are clear and there is no peripheral edema.
Client walks to the mailbox and back each day without becoming short of breath.
Client states, 'My daughter calls every evening to check on me.'
Client verbalizes the purpose of each medication in the organizer.

items.rationale: Falls entering the tub and inability to open pill bottles are function and home safety problems that occupational therapy resolves with transfer equipment, adaptive openers and a home assessment. A diet of canned soup and lunch meat delivers a sodium load that will drive a heart failure exacerbation, so the dietitian is involved before the next admission. Daily walking without dyspnea is a strength to reinforce, not a problem.

items.stem: Click to highlight the entries that should not appear in the client's medical record following a medication error.

highlightSegments.text: 1500 Client received metoprolol 50 mg by mouth that had been prepared for another client.
Heart rate 58 and blood pressure 104/62 mm Hg; client denies dizziness or chest pain.
Provider notified at 1510; orders received to monitor vital signs every 30 minutes for 4 hours.
Occurrence report completed and forwarded to risk management.
The error happened because the night nurse left unlabeled medications on the counter.
1530 Heart rate 62, blood pressure 110/66 mm Hg; client alert and oriented.
Family was not informed of the error, per the charge nurse's instruction.
1600 Client resting comfortably; vital signs remain at the client's baseline.
This would not have happened if the unit were staffed properly.
1630 Client ambulated in the hallway without dizziness; no further orders received.

items.rationale: The chart documents what the client received, the client's response, who was notified and what was ordered, all in objective terms. It never names the occurrence report, which is a protected internal quality document, and it never carries blame, speculation about cause or complaints about staffing; those belong in the report and the review that follows. Recording that the family was deliberately not told documents a decision that conflicts with disclosure policy.

items.stem: A nurse reviews the unit's central line quality data for the past 4 months. Which findings in the trended data indicate that central line care on the unit is deteriorating? Select all that apply.
options: The rise in infections is explained by the increase in line days
Dressing audit pass rates have fallen by more than 30 percentage points
The number of bloodstream infections has risen every month
Chlorhexidine bathing compliance has declined steadily
Central line days have increased sharply over the 4 months
Fewer clients on the unit now have central lines
items.rationale: Two process measures, dressing integrity and chlorhexidine bathing, fall month after month while the infection count rises, which is the signature of eroding practice rather than changing case mix. Line days stay essentially flat between 318 and 330, so exposure has not increased and cannot account for the infections. Reading the process measures alongside the outcome is what tells the unit where to intervene, in this case on dressing maintenance and daily bathing.

items.stem: For each client need, select the team member the nurse should involve.
matrixRows: Client with a new colostomy needs help selecting and applying pouching supplies.
Family asks for a blessing before life-sustaining treatment is withdrawn.
Client needs authorization for a skilled nursing facility bed after discharge.
Client starting hemodialysis asks which foods are highest in potassium.
Client's stage 4 pressure injury needs a revised treatment plan and accurate staging documentation.
Client cannot afford the monthly cost of home oxygen and needs benefits reviewed.
items.rationale: Ostomy pouching and pressure injury staging and treatment are both within the wound, ostomy and continence nurse's specialty, while the case manager handles authorizations, placement and benefits questions that determine whether the plan is affordable. Renal diet teaching belongs to the dietitian, and spiritual rituals at the end of life to chaplaincy. Sending each need to the right discipline the first time shortens the delay before the client's problem is actually solved.

items.stem: A client is being discharged with home oxygen, a walker, and orders for home health dressing changes. For each client statement, select whether it demonstrates understanding or indicates that further teaching is needed.
matrixRows: 'The home health nurse will come on Tuesday and Friday to change my dressing.'
'I can smoke in the other room as long as the oxygen stays in the bedroom.'
'I will call the equipment company when the rubber tips on my walker wear down.'
'If I run out of dressing supplies, I will use a clean washcloth until the next visit.'
'My follow-up appointment with the surgeon is on my calendar for next Wednesday.'
'I will stop taking the antibiotic once the drainage from the wound looks better.'
items.rationale: Knowing the visit schedule, maintaining the walker and keeping the follow-up appointment show the client can carry out the plan. Smoking anywhere in a home with oxygen is a fire risk regardless of which room the concentrator is in, and oxygen fires usually start with exactly this reasoning. A washcloth is not a substitute for sterile supplies, and stopping an antibiotic early promotes resistance and relapse.

items.stem: A nurse discovers that a client has just been given a medication intended for another client. Place the steps in the correct order.
options: Carry out the monitoring and treatment ordered by the prescriber.
Notify the prescriber and the charge nurse that the wrong medication was given.
Document the medication given, the provider notification and the client's response in the medical record.
Assess the client and obtain a full set of vital signs.
Complete the facility's occurrence report and forward it to risk management.
items.rationale: The client's safety comes before any paperwork, so assessment and vital signs are first and determine how urgent everything that follows is. The prescriber and charge nurse are notified next because orders and additional resources flow from that call, then the ordered monitoring or treatment is carried out. Charting the facts and the client's response completes the medical record, and the occurrence report, which is a separate internal document, is filed last.

items.stem: A client is being transferred from the med-surg unit to a skilled nursing facility. Place the steps in the correct order.
options: Send the medical records, personal belongings and prescribed equipment with the client.
Verify the transfer orders and complete the transfer summary with the reconciled medication list.
Document the time of transfer, the mode of transport and the client's condition on departure.
Give the receiving nurse a verbal SBAR handoff and allow time for questions.
Confirm that the receiving facility has accepted the client and that a bed has been assigned.
items.rationale: Nothing else in a transfer matters until the receiving facility has formally accepted the client and holds a bed, because a client who arrives without an assigned bed may be sent back. The transfer summary with reconciled medications is prepared next, then the verbal SBAR handoff, which is the only step that lets the receiving nurse ask questions before responsibility shifts. Records, belongings and equipment travel with the client, and the departure entry closes the sending unit's record.

items.stem: A charge nurse reviews the discharge plan for an 84-year-old client who had a hip hemiarthroplasty 4 days ago. The client lives alone, has three steps at the only entrance to the home, has fallen twice in the past 6 months, and still needs assistance to rise from a chair. Complete the diagram by selecting the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess progress.
bowtieConditions: Ineffective coping with the surgical outcome
Risk for injury from an unsafe discharge environment
Nonadherence to the prescribed medication regimen
bowtieActions: Ask the family to hire a private caregiver before the client is discharged
Arrange a chaplain visit before the client leaves the unit
Request an occupational therapy home safety evaluation and equipment training before discharge
Discharge as planned and provide written fall-prevention instructions
Request a case management consult for skilled home health and durable medical equipment
bowtieParams: The client's ability to transfer and ambulate safely with the prescribed walker
Delivery and correct use of the prescribed equipment in the home
items.rationale: Living alone with entry steps, a fall history and dependence for transfers describes an environment the client cannot yet navigate safely, which is a discharge planning problem rather than a cognitive, adherence or coping one. The remedy is coordination before discharge: case management for home health and equipment, and occupational therapy to evaluate the home and train the client with it. Readiness is judged by demonstrated safe transfers and by equipment that has arrived and is used correctly.

items.stem: A nurse on a medical-surgical unit is planning the shift with an experienced assistive personnel (AP). Which task is most appropriate for the nurse to delegate to the AP?
options: Teaching a client newly diagnosed with diabetes how to use an insulin pen
Ambulating a client who is 2 days postoperative from an open appendectomy and has been walking in the hallway without difficulty
Deciding whether a client's pain improved enough after the last dose of oxycodone
Completing the admission history for a client who has just arrived from the emergency department
items.rationale: Ambulating a stable client along a predictable, established routine is a standard task within the assistive personnel role. An admission history is an initial assessment, teaching a new skill requires assessing readiness and understanding, and judging whether an intervention worked is evaluation. Assessment, teaching and evaluation are nursing judgment and remain with the registered nurse.

items.stem: A charge nurse is making assignments on a medical-surgical unit and has one LPN/LVN on the team. Which client is most appropriate to assign to the LPN/LVN?
options: A client receiving the first dose of IV vancomycin
A client who arrived 30 minutes ago with abdominal pain and has not yet been assessed
A client who needs discharge teaching before starting a new anticoagulant at home
A client with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease receiving scheduled nebulizer treatments and oral prednisone
items.rationale: An LPN/LVN may care for a stable client with a predictable course and give routine oral and inhaled medications. A client who has not yet been assessed requires the RN's initial assessment, first-dose IV antibiotics require the RN to monitor for a reaction, and initial discharge teaching requires assessment of learning needs. The RN keeps assessment, teaching and the unpredictable client.

items.stem: A charge nurse on a medical-surgical unit receives a nurse floated from the postpartum unit for the shift. Which client should the charge nurse assign to the floated nurse?
options: A client with continuous bladder irrigation after a transurethral resection of the prostate
A client 2 hours after a thoracotomy with a newly placed chest tube
A client with new-onset atrial fibrillation receiving an IV amiodarone infusion
A client with cellulitis of the lower leg receiving IV antibiotics who is afebrile and ambulatory
items.rationale: A floated nurse is given clients whose care falls within skills common to all nursing practice, such as IV antibiotics and routine monitoring of a stable client. A fresh chest tube, a titrated antiarrhythmic infusion and continuous bladder irrigation all require unit-specific competencies the postpartum nurse is unlikely to hold. Assigning outside a nurse's demonstrated competence is unsafe even when the nurse is experienced.

items.stem: A nurse observes assistive personnel preparing to move a client up in bed by placing both hands under the client's axillae and pulling. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Stop the move and demonstrate use of a friction-reducing slide sheet with two staff members
Ask the assistive personnel to explain why that method was chosen
Document the observation in the client's record
Report the assistive personnel to the nurse manager at the end of the shift
items.rationale: Supervision includes intervening at once when delegated care is being done unsafely. Pulling under the axillae risks brachial plexus injury and shears the skin, so the nurse stops the move and models the correct technique. Documenting, reporting to the manager, or exploring the rationale may follow, but none of them protects this client in the moment.

items.stem: A home health nurse coordinates care for a client with heart failure who is visited three times a week by a home health aide. Which task is appropriate for the nurse to delegate to the aide?
options: Adjusting the client's daily fluid limit based on the reported weight
Weighing the client each morning on the same scale and recording the weight
Deciding whether the client should take the as-needed dose of furosemide
Listening to the client's lungs for crackles at each visit
items.rationale: Obtaining and recording a daily weight is a standard, unchanging measurement that an aide can perform and report. Deciding about a diuretic dose, auscultating lungs and changing a fluid restriction all require assessment and nursing judgment. The nurse uses the aide's reported data but keeps the interpretation and the decisions.

items.stem: A school nurse covers three campuses and is planning care for a 7-year-old student with type 1 diabetes who uses an insulin pump. Which responsibility may the nurse delegate to trained unlicensed school personnel?
options: Assessing the student when the pump site alarms and deciding whether the site must be changed
Determining the correction dose to enter into the pump when the glucose is elevated
Supervising the student's mid-morning snack and reporting any symptoms of hypoglycemia to the nurse
Teaching the classroom teacher to recognize diabetic ketoacidosis
items.rationale: Trained unlicensed school personnel may carry out routine, predictable supervision and report observations back to the nurse. Calculating an insulin correction dose, assessing an alarming pump site and teaching staff about a complication all require nursing knowledge and judgment. Delegation transfers the task, never the accountability or the assessment behind it.

items.stem: A nurse delegates vital sign measurement for four stable clients to assistive personnel. Which direction by the nurse best demonstrates the right direction and communication?
options: 'Get the vital signs whenever you can and chart them before the end of the shift.'
'You have done this many times, so just handle the vital signs the way you usually do.'
'Take everyone's vital signs sometime this morning and let me know if anything looks off.'
'Check vital signs in rooms 12 through 15 by 0900, and tell me right away if any systolic pressure is below 100 or any heart rate is above 110.'
items.rationale: The right direction and communication means the delegated task is described specifically, with a deadline and explicit parameters for reporting back. Vague phrases such as 'sometime this morning' or 'if anything looks off' leave the assistive personnel to decide what is abnormal, which is nursing judgment. Assuming experience substitutes for clear instruction is a common cause of missed deterioration.

items.stem: A preceptor is choosing an assignment for a new graduate nurse in the sixth week of orientation on a medical-surgical unit. Which client is most appropriate?
options: A client with community-acquired pneumonia on oral antibiotics who is being prepared for discharge tomorrow
A client 1 hour after femoral angiography who requires frequent groin site checks
A client who is actively dying while the family debates withdrawing life support
A client with diabetic ketoacidosis receiving an insulin infusion with hourly glucose checks
items.rationale: An orientee is assigned clients whose conditions are stable and whose care matches skills already demonstrated, with the preceptor available for support. Titrated insulin infusions, a fresh arterial access site and a family in crisis over end-of-life decisions all demand rapid, experienced judgment. Building competence in graded steps protects both the client and the new nurse.

items.stem: A nurse is planning the shift on a medical-surgical unit. Which tasks may the nurse delegate to assistive personnel? Select all that apply.
options: Recording oral intake and urinary output for a client with heart failure
Performing the first postoperative dressing change on an abdominal incision
Assisting a stable client with a bed bath
Determining whether a client is ready to be discharged home
Collecting a clean-catch urine specimen from a client who can follow directions
Transporting a stable client to the radiology department by wheelchair
items.rationale: Hygiene, transport, measured intake and output, and specimen collection on a stable client are routine tasks with predictable outcomes and are within the assistive personnel role. The first postoperative dressing change requires the nurse to assess the incision, and readiness for discharge is an evaluation of the plan of care. Both of those require nursing judgment and cannot be delegated.

items.stem: A charge nurse is reviewing which responsibilities must be kept by the registered nurse rather than assigned to an LPN/LVN. Which responsibilities are retained by the RN? Select all that apply.
options: Performing the initial admission assessment on a newly arrived client
Initiating a transfusion of packed red blood cells
Providing the first teaching session for a newly prescribed insulin regimen
Developing the client's plan of care
Administering a scheduled oral antihypertensive
Changing a clean dressing on a healing surgical wound
items.rationale: The RN owns the nursing process: the initial assessment, the plan of care, initial teaching and evaluation. Initiating blood products is also an RN function in most states because the first minutes carry the risk of a transfusion reaction. Scheduled oral medications and routine dressing changes on a stable client are squarely within LPN/LVN practice.

items.stem: A nurse manager is evaluating a charge nurse's delegation practice during a shift. Which observations indicate that the five rights of delegation were applied correctly? Select all that apply.
options: The charge nurse rounded at midshift to watch the delegated task being performed
The charge nurse confirmed that the assistive personnel had been trained and checked off on the mechanical lift before assigning transfers
The charge nurse stated the exact glucose value at which the assistive personnel must call the nurse
The charge nurse assigned a client with unstable vital signs to the assistive personnel because that person knew the client well
The charge nurse reviewed the recorded intake and output with the assistive personnel before the end of the shift
The charge nurse asked the assistive personnel to chart a description of the client's lung sounds
items.rationale: Verifying training addresses the right person, naming the exact value to report addresses the right direction, watching the task addresses the right supervision, and reviewing the results addresses evaluation. Assigning an unstable client fails the right circumstance, because delegated tasks belong to clients with predictable outcomes. Describing lung sounds is assessment and is never the right task for assistive personnel.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: In a long-term care facility, assistive personnel report that a resident who is normally alert and oriented is now confused and has tried to climb over the side rail. The nurse should first {{1}}, and should recognize that this change means the resident's care now {{2}}.

options: assess the resident and look for causes such as infection, hypoxia, pain or a new medication
ask the assistive personnel to move the resident to a room near the nurses' station
document the report and recheck the resident at the end of the shift
direct the assistive personnel to apply a vest restraint for safety
can be delegated with more frequent neurologic checks by the assistive personnel
no longer meets the right circumstance for routine delegation and needs nursing assessment
should be transferred to another unit before any assessment is done
must be documented as a behavioral problem rather than a clinical change

items.rationale: A sudden change in mental status is an acute clinical cue, so the nurse assesses the resident for reversible causes such as urinary infection, hypoxia, pain or a recent medication change. Once a client stops being stable and predictable, the right circumstance for delegation is gone and the nurse resumes direct monitoring. Restraints are never the first response, and delaying the assessment ignores a warning sign.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A charge nurse sees an LPN/LVN on a telemetry unit drawing up IV push labetalol for a client whose blood pressure is 198/104 mm Hg. The charge nurse should {{1}}, because giving intravenous push medications is {{2}}.

options: ask a second LPN/LVN to verify the dose before it is given
stop the LPN/LVN and administer the dose personally after checking the blood pressure
wait until the dose is given and then notify the nurse manager
let the LPN/LVN give the dose while the charge nurse observes
outside the LPN/LVN scope of practice in most states
allowed whenever a registered nurse is in the room
left to the charge nurse's discretion during busy shifts
permitted for LPNs/LVNs only with antibiotics

items.rationale: In most states an LPN/LVN may not administer intravenous push medications, and a vasoactive drug such as labetalol demands continuous registered nurse assessment of blood pressure and heart rate. Supervision requires intervening before harm occurs rather than observing, verifying with a second LPN/LVN, or reporting afterward. Scope of practice is set by the state board, not by staffing pressure.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A night charge nurse has one registered nurse, one LPN/LVN and two assistive personnel for 14 clients, including a client 4 hours after carotid endarterectomy and a client receiving a titrated heparin infusion. The postoperative client should be assigned to {{1}}, and the LPN/LVN should be assigned {{2}}.

options: the registered nurse, who can perform the frequent neurovascular and airway assessments
the LPN/LVN, who can measure vital signs every hour
whichever staff member finishes the medication pass first
assistive personnel, with the registered nurse checking in each hour
the two clients still waiting for admission assessments
stable clients needing scheduled oral medications and routine wound care
the discharge teaching for a client starting warfarin at home
the heparin infusion, including rate titration for the ordered range

items.rationale: A client hours after carotid surgery can develop neck hematoma, airway compromise or stroke, so the registered nurse performs those assessments. Titrating a heparin infusion, admission assessments and initial anticoagulation teaching all require RN judgment as well. Assigning the LPN/LVN a group of stable clients with routine medications and wound care matches the staff mix to acuity.

items.stem: Click to highlight the statements in the assistive personnel's end-of-shift report that require the nurse to assess the client before this care continues to be delegated.

highlightSegments.text: 1500 report from assistive personnel on a 74-year-old client admitted with pneumonia.
Client ate 75% of lunch and drank 240 mL of water.
Client became short of breath and had to sit down halfway down the hallway while walking.
Bed bath completed; skin is intact except for a reddened area over the sacrum that does not blanch.
Client used the urinal three times during the shift.
Vital signs at 1400: temperature 37.2 C (99 F), heart rate 92, blood pressure 128/74, respirations 18.
Client coughed while sipping water, so more sips were offered through a straw.
Client asked that the head of the bed stay elevated.
Family brought in slippers with nonskid soles.
Client said the pain medicine from this morning 'took the edge off.'

items.rationale: New shortness of breath with activity, a nonblanchable reddened sacrum and coughing while drinking are all cues the nurse must evaluate personally: they signal activity intolerance, a stage 1 pressure injury and possible aspiration risk. Offering a straw after coughing also increases aspiration risk and must be corrected. Intake, voiding, stable vital signs, positioning preference and nonskid footwear are expected findings that need no urgent follow-up.

items.stem: An experienced charge nurse reviews the assignment a new charge nurse wrote for the LPN/LVN. Click to highlight the parts of the assignment that fall outside the LPN/LVN scope of practice and must be reassigned.

highlightSegments.text: Day shift assignment for the LPN/LVN, rooms 20 through 24:
Give the scheduled oral and subcutaneous medications for all five rooms.
Complete the admission assessment on the client arriving from the emergency department at 0900.
Change the clean dressing on the healing abdominal wound in room 21.
Insert the indwelling urinary catheter prescribed for room 23.
Start the unit of packed red blood cells for the client in room 22.
Reinforce the low-sodium diet teaching that the registered nurse began yesterday.
Give IV push hydromorphone for breakthrough pain in room 20.
Record intake and output and report any urine output under 30 mL/hr.
Write the plan of care for the client newly admitted with a stroke.

items.rationale: Initial admission assessment, starting blood products, IV push medications and writing the plan of care are registered nurse responsibilities in most states and must be reassigned. Routine oral and subcutaneous medications, clean dressing changes, catheter insertion, reinforcement of teaching already begun by the RN, and measured intake and output are all within LPN/LVN practice. The dividing line is nursing judgment, not task difficulty.

items.stem: Assistive personnel recorded the vital signs below for a client 1 day after a colon resection. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The client is showing signs of sepsis; the nurse must assess the client and notify the provider now
The client is anxious about going home and needs reassurance and rest
The changes are an expected postoperative response and vital signs may continue every 4 hours
The assistive personnel should recheck the blood pressure in the opposite arm before the nurse is involved
items.rationale: Rising temperature with climbing heart rate and respirations and a falling blood pressure is the classic trajectory of sepsis after bowel surgery, and it needs immediate nurse assessment and provider notification. Vital signs may be delegated only while a client stays stable, and the nurse should have been called at 1200 when the parameters were crossed. Repeating the measurement or attributing the change to anxiety delays treatment during the most time-sensitive hours.

items.stem: A nurse manager reviews unit data 5 months after introducing a delegation checklist and structured hourly rounding by assistive personnel. Which conclusion is supported by the trend?
options: The data show the unit is understaffed and rounding should be stopped
The delegation changes are producing sustained improvement and should be continued
Turning should no longer be delegated because pressure injuries are increasing
The drop in falls is unrelated to the changes, so the checklist should be discontinued
items.rationale: Every indicator moves in the same favorable direction across three consecutive measurement points, which supports continuing the practice change. Evaluating the outcome of delegated work is the registered nurse's responsibility and the final step of the delegation process. Pressure injuries fell rather than rose, and nothing in the data suggests rounding caused harm or that staffing worsened.

items.stem: A charge nurse is deciding who should carry out each task on a medical-surgical unit. Indicate the most appropriate staff member for each task.
matrixRows: Assisting a stable client to the bathroom
Administering a scheduled oral stool softener
Writing the plan of care for a newly admitted client
Measuring and recording the daily weight
Performing tracheostomy care on a well-established tracheostomy
Evaluating a client's response to a newly started antihypertensive
items.rationale: Assistive personnel carry out routine, standardized care such as toileting a stable client and obtaining a weight. LPNs/LVNs give routine oral medications and perform established procedures such as tracheostomy care on a mature stoma. Writing the plan of care and evaluating the response to a new medication require assessment and clinical judgment, so they stay with the registered nurse.

items.stem: A nurse sees assistive personnel carry a shared glucometer directly from one client's room into another client's room without cleaning it. Place the steps in the correct order.
options: Explain that a shared glucometer must be disinfected between clients because it can transmit bloodborne pathogens.
Document the corrective teaching and inform the nurse manager of the practice gap.
Have the device disinfected with the approved wipe for the full contact time.
Stop the assistive personnel before the glucometer touches the second client.
Observe the assistive personnel perform the next glucose check correctly.
items.rationale: Supervision starts with stopping the unsafe act before the second client is exposed. The nurse then explains the reason for disinfection so the correction is understood, has the device cleaned for the required contact time, and watches the next check to confirm the change. Documenting and informing the manager close the loop but come last, because they do nothing to protect the client at the bedside.

items.stem: An emergency department charge nurse is assigning clients in the fast-track area, where one LPN/LVN works under registered nurse supervision. Which client is most appropriate to assign to the LPN/LVN?
options: A client with an allergic reaction who is receiving intramuscular epinephrine
A client who needs the initial assessment after a low-speed motor vehicle crash
A client whose forearm laceration has just been sutured and who needs the wound cleaned and a sterile dressing applied
A client who has arrived by private car with chest pain and needs to be triaged
items.rationale: Wound care and dressing application after a provider has repaired a laceration is a routine, standardized procedure within LPN/LVN practice. Triage is an assessment-driven decision about acuity and belongs to the registered nurse, as does the initial assessment of any new arrival. A client actively being treated for an allergic reaction is unstable and needs continuous RN evaluation.

items.stem: A nurse in the intensive care unit is caring for a client receiving mechanical ventilation. Which task may the nurse delegate to assistive personnel?
options: Performing oral care with the unit's protocol swabs every 2 hours
Measuring the endotracheal tube cuff pressure
Adjusting the ventilator alarm limits after a desaturation event
Suctioning the endotracheal tube whenever the client coughs
items.rationale: Oral care using a standardized protocol is routine hygiene and is delegated to assistive personnel even for a ventilated client, and it reduces ventilator-associated pneumonia. Suctioning requires assessing breath sounds and tolerating the procedure, cuff pressure measurement requires interpretation, and ventilator settings belong to the registered nurse and respiratory therapist. Being in a critical care unit does not change what may be delegated; the nature of the task does.

items.stem: A charge nurse walks into a room and finds an LPN/LVN spiking a unit of packed red blood cells that has just arrived from the blood bank. Which action should the charge nurse take?
options: Send the unit back to the blood bank and reschedule the transfusion for the next shift
Let the infusion start and stay in the room for the first 15 minutes
Direct the LPN/LVN to complete the two-person verification with a second LPN/LVN
Take over the transfusion, perform the verification, start the infusion, and review the policy with the LPN/LVN
items.rationale: In most states initiating a blood product is a registered nurse function because the first 15 minutes carry the highest risk of a hemolytic or anaphylactic reaction that must be assessed and treated immediately. The charge nurse assumes the task now and teaches afterward, which is supervision rather than discipline. Verification by two LPNs/LVNs does not make the act legal, and returning a released unit wastes a resource and delays needed treatment.

items.stem: A telehealth nursing service is staffed by registered nurses and LPNs/LVNs. Which call is appropriate for the LPN/LVN to handle without involving a registered nurse?
options: A parent asking whether a 4-month-old with a temperature of 39 C (102.2 F) needs an urgent visit
A client asking whether a new rash after starting an antibiotic means the drug should be stopped
A client asking to confirm the clinic's walk-in influenza vaccine hours and location
A client describing chest tightness that began while mowing the lawn
items.rationale: Confirming published hours and a location is factual information that requires no assessment, so it is within the LPN/LVN role. Every other call is telephone triage: deciding the urgency of an infant's fever, evaluating exertional chest tightness or judging a possible drug reaction all require gathering and interpreting assessment data. Telephone triage is a registered nurse function because the decision itself is nursing judgment.

items.stem: A registered nurse leads a primary care clinic team that includes a medical assistant and an LPN/LVN. A client arrives for an annual visit. Which task should the nurse assign to the medical assistant?
options: Administering the depression screening tool and interpreting the resulting score
Recording the client's height, weight and vital signs before the provider's visit
Explaining how and when to take a newly prescribed metformin
Reconciling the client's home medication list and resolving the discrepancies found
items.rationale: Obtaining standard measurements is a routine, objective task well within the medical assistant role. Medication reconciliation involves judgment about discrepancies, teaching about a new drug requires assessing understanding, and interpreting a screening score is clinical evaluation. The measurements the medical assistant obtains still have to be reviewed and acted on by a licensed nurse.

items.stem: Assistive personnel tell the nurse that a client who is 1 day after total hip arthroplasty 'just does not seem right today and did not want to get out of bed.' Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Ask the assistive personnel to try to get the client up again in an hour
Document that the client declined the prescribed activity
Call the provider to report that the client is refusing to ambulate
Go to the room and assess the client, including mental status, oxygen saturation and the operative leg
items.rationale: A vague concern from staff who see the client all shift is a legitimate cue, and after hip surgery a change in behavior can signal pulmonary embolism, fat embolism, hypoxia, bleeding or delirium. Supervision means acting on what delegated staff report, so the nurse assesses before drawing conclusions. Repeating the attempt, calling the provider without data, or charting a refusal all skip the assessment that determines what is actually wrong.

items.stem: A nurse delegates a bed bath and 2-hour repositioning to assistive personnel and learns at the end of the shift that the repositioning was never done. Which statement reflects the nurse's accountability?
options: No one is accountable because repositioning is only a comfort measure
The assistive personnel is solely responsible because the task was accepted
The nurse remains accountable for the outcome of delegated care and for verifying that it was completed
Accountability passed to the charge nurse when the assignment was made
items.rationale: Delegation transfers the performance of a task but never the accountability for the outcome, so the nurse is responsible for supervising and verifying that repositioning occurred. Assistive personnel are responsible for their own actions and for reporting what they did or could not do, which is shared responsibility rather than a transfer. Repositioning prevents pressure injury and is a required intervention, not an optional comfort measure.

items.stem: A charge nurse greets an agency nurse who has never worked on the unit and who states being unfamiliar with the unit's insulin infusion protocol. Which action should the charge nurse take?
options: Have the agency nurse work as assistive personnel for the shift
Assign clients who do not require titrated infusions and pair the agency nurse with a unit nurse as a resource
Give the usual six-client group and tell the agency nurse to read the protocol during the shift
Send the agency nurse home and ask unit staff to stay for overtime
items.rationale: Assignments must match a nurse's demonstrated competence, so a nurse unfamiliar with a titration protocol is given clients within general medical-surgical practice and a named resource person. Handing over the standard group and expecting self-teaching during care puts clients at risk. Sending a licensed nurse home worsens the staffing problem, and asking a registered nurse to work below license wastes the license and may violate the agency contract.

items.stem: A nurse is delegating the first ambulation of the day for a client who is 1 day after abdominal surgery. Which instructions should the nurse give the assistive personnel? Select all that apply.
options: Tell me right away if the client becomes dizzy, short of breath or reports chest pain
Give the as-needed pain medication first if the client says it is needed
Walk the client to the end of the hall and back, and stop if the client cannot continue
Decide how far the client should walk based on how the client looks
Apply the gait belt and have a second staff member available for this first walk
Secure the surgical drain and the IV tubing before the client stands
items.rationale: Effective direction states the exact task and its limits, the equipment and help required, and the findings that must be reported back at once. Deciding how far a postoperative client should walk is an assessment-based judgment that stays with the nurse, and assistive personnel do not administer medication of any kind. Clear parameters are what allow a delegated activity to be stopped safely before harm occurs.

items.stem: A registered nurse supervises an LPN/LVN in a long-term care facility. Which tasks are within the LPN/LVN's scope of practice? Select all that apply.
options: Completing the comprehensive admission assessment for a new resident
Writing the resident's individualized care plan for the quarterly review
Suctioning the oropharynx of a resident with a chronic tracheostomy
Administering routine scheduled subcutaneous insulin
Performing a gastrostomy tube feeding through an established tube
Reinforcing transfer technique teaching that the registered nurse began
items.rationale: LPNs/LVNs give routine subcutaneous and oral medications, perform established procedures such as tube feedings and suctioning, and reinforce teaching the registered nurse has already started. The comprehensive admission assessment and the care plan are the registered nurse's responsibility because both require gathering and interpreting data to set the direction of care. The LPN/LVN contributes observations to the plan but does not author it.

items.stem: A nurse manager reviews a shift in which delegated care went wrong. Which findings point to a failure of nursing supervision rather than an error by the assistive personnel? Select all that apply.
options: The nurse did not look at any delegated glucose results until the end of the shift
The nurse assigned monitoring of a client on a titrated insulin infusion to assistive personnel
The nurse never stated how often the client on bed rest was to be repositioned
The nurse did not verify whether the newly hired assistive personnel had been trained on the mechanical lift
The assistive personnel recorded the client's intake in the record after each meal
The assistive personnel measured the blood pressure with an appropriately sized cuff
items.rationale: Omitting the frequency of a task fails the right direction, ignoring results until the shift ends fails the right supervision and evaluation, delegating an unstable client fails the right circumstance, and not confirming training fails the right person. Using the correct cuff and charting intake promptly are examples of delegated care done correctly. Naming which right was broken points the manager toward a system fix instead of individual blame.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: During perineal care for a client with an indwelling urinary catheter, the nurse sees assistive personnel lift the drainage bag onto the bed above the level of the client's bladder. The nurse should {{1}}, and should explain that the bag stays below the bladder in order to {{2}}.

options: wait until the care is finished and mention it at the end of the shift
empty the drainage bag and continue to watch without comment
have the tubing clamped for the remainder of the bath
intervene now and have the bag lowered and secured to the bed frame
reduce traction on the catheter balloon
keep the tubing from kinking while the client is turned
make hourly urine measurement easier to read
keep urine from draining back into the bladder and causing infection

items.rationale: Raising the collection bag above the bladder allows contaminated urine to flow back and is a leading cause of catheter-associated urinary tract infection, so the nurse corrects it immediately rather than later. Clamping the tubing creates stasis and is not a substitute. Supervision of delegated care means stopping the unsafe step at the bedside and explaining the reason so the practice actually changes.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: An oncology unit receives a nurse floated from the emergency department who holds no chemotherapy certification. The charge nurse should assign this nurse {{1}}, and should make sure that {{2}} stays with a chemotherapy-certified nurse.

options: clients needing symptom management, hydration and routine IV antibiotics
the client starting the first cycle of a vesicant infusion
every admission that arrives during the shift
the clients whose charts require the least documentation
the hourly rounding schedule
the controlled substance count for the unit
administration and monitoring of all chemotherapy infusions
the discharge paperwork for the shift

items.rationale: Floating is safe only when the assignment falls within skills the nurse already holds; hydration, antibiotics and symptom management are general medical-surgical competencies. Hazardous drug administration requires specific certification because of extravasation, hypersensitivity and exposure risks, so it stays with a certified nurse. Choosing the assignment by documentation load or handing over all admissions ignores competence entirely.

items.stem: A nurse manager reviews a novice nurse's narrative note describing how the shift was delegated. Click to highlight the parts of the note that describe unsafe delegation and require the manager to intervene.

highlightSegments.text: 1930 note by the nurse assigned to rooms 30 through 35.
I asked the assistive personnel to obtain vital signs on all six clients every 4 hours.
I told the assistive personnel to call me for any temperature above 38 C (100.4 F) or heart rate above 110.
I asked the assistive personnel to decide whether the client in room 32 was in enough pain to need medication.
I assigned the bed bath and linen change in room 30 to the assistive personnel.
I gave the float nurse the client in room 34 who is 2 hours post thyroidectomy with hourly airway checks.
I asked the LPN/LVN to give the scheduled oral medications for rooms 33 and 35.
I asked the LPN/LVN to complete the admission assessment on the client arriving at 2000.
I reviewed the recorded vital signs at 2100 along with the intake and output totals.
I asked the assistive personnel to tell the family in room 31 that I would come in after the medication pass.

items.rationale: Judging whether a client needs pain medication is assessment and cannot be delegated, a client hours after thyroidectomy needs airway assessment by a nurse competent in that care, and the admission assessment belongs to the registered nurse. Measuring vital signs with stated report-back parameters, hygiene, scheduled oral medications and reviewing recorded data are appropriate. Unsafe delegation is identified by the judgment a task requires, not by how busy the shift was.

items.stem: A client who is 3 days after hip surgery describes the night shift to the day nurse. Click to highlight the statements that indicate a problem with delegation or supervision requiring the nurse's follow-up.

highlightSegments.text: 0715: The client gives an account of the night to the oncoming nurse.
'The aide helped me wash up around ten and was very kind about it.'
'Nobody came to turn me between midnight and six, and my back was burning by morning.'
'The aide told me my blood pressure was low but said it was nothing to worry about.'
'I got my pain medicine around two in the morning and slept after that.'
'The aide unhooked my oxygen tubing so I could walk to the bathroom, and I felt out of breath.'
'They brought me ice water whenever I asked for it.'
'My call light stayed within reach all night.'
'The aide emptied my urinal and wrote the amount down.'
'I walked to the chair this morning with the aide and the gait belt.'

items.rationale: Six hours without repositioning is omitted care that risks a pressure injury, and interpreting a low blood pressure as unimportant instead of reporting it exceeds the assistive personnel role. Removing prescribed oxygen is a change in therapy that only a nurse may decide, and the resulting breathlessness needs assessment now. Hygiene, pain medication given by a nurse, fluids, a call light in reach, recorded output and a gait-belt walk all show care delivered as planned.

items.stem: Assistive personnel recorded the daily weights and fluid totals below for a client with heart failure on a telemetry unit. Which action should the nurse take first based on the trend?
options: Assess the client for worsening fluid overload and notify the provider
Encourage the client to drink more fluids to improve the urine output
Document the values and continue the current plan of care
Ask the assistive personnel to reweigh the client on a different scale
items.rationale: A 3.2 kg gain over 2 days with output falling well below intake represents roughly 3 L of retained fluid and signals decompensating heart failure. Data gathered by assistive personnel is valid, but interpreting it and acting on it are nursing responsibilities, so the nurse assesses for crackles, edema and dyspnea and notifies the provider. Repeating the weight, increasing fluids or simply charting the numbers all delay treatment.

items.stem: In a long-term care facility, assistive personnel recorded the point-of-care glucose values below for a resident whose prednisone is being tapered. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The assistive personnel is measuring the glucose incorrectly and needs retraining
The resident is developing type 2 diabetes and needs a long-acting insulin added
The glucose values are falling as the steroid is tapered, so the sliding-scale coverage should be reviewed with the provider
The values are unrelated to the prednisone and require no nursing action
items.rationale: Corticosteroids raise glucose, and as the dose tapers the hyperglycemia resolves, so unchanged sliding-scale insulin sets the resident up for hypoglycemia. The nurse's role is to review the delegated results, recognize the pattern and ask the provider to adjust the orders. The steady, dose-related decline argues against a new diabetes diagnosis and against measurement error, and taking no action ignores an avoidable risk.

items.stem: A nurse overhears the statements below from assistive personnel during the shift. Indicate whether each statement requires the nurse to follow up.
matrixRows: 'I helped the client onto the bedpan and then recorded the urine output.'
'I told the client in room 12 that the new chest pain was probably just gas.'
'I used the mechanical lift by myself because the other aide was at lunch.'
'I raised the head of the bed before I set up the lunch tray.'
'The blood pressure was 84/50, so I rechecked it and got the same reading.'
'I put the compression stockings back on after the bath.'
items.rationale: Interpreting chest pain as harmless is assessment outside the assistive personnel role and could delay care for a coronary event, a one-person mechanical lift transfer violates safe handling policy, and an abnormal blood pressure confirmed on recheck must be reported rather than simply repeated. Recording output, elevating the head of the bed for a meal and reapplying compression stockings are correct delegated care.

items.stem: Assistive personnel call out that a client is sitting on the floor beside the bed. Place the nurse's actions in the correct order.
options: Notify the provider and the client's family according to facility policy.
Go to the room and assess level of consciousness, vital signs and any injury before the client is moved.
Complete the incident report and document the assessment and interventions in the record.
Begin the neurologic and vital sign checks required after an unwitnessed fall.
Return the client to bed with enough staff and place the call light and needed items within reach.
Ask the assistive personnel what happened and whether the client was lowered to the floor.
items.rationale: The client is assessed for injury before being moved, because moving a client with a possible fracture or head injury can worsen it. The account from the assistive personnel establishes whether the fall was witnessed and guides monitoring, then the client is returned to bed safely and placed on post-fall checks. Provider and family notification and the incident report follow; the report is a quality document and is never referenced in the chart.

items.stem: Assistive personnel report that a client who is 3 days after a hysterectomy 'feels hot and is breathing fast.' The nurse assesses the client and finds temperature 38.9 C (102 F), heart rate 124/min, respirations 28/min, blood pressure 88/52 mm Hg, skin flushed and warm, and only 60 mL of urine in the past 3 hours; the assistive personnel had not measured vital signs since 0800. Complete the diagram by selecting the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess progress.
bowtieActions: Ask the assistive personnel to take vital signs every 4 hours and report back
Obtain blood cultures and give the prescribed broad-spectrum antibiotic within 1 hour
Hold all intravenous fluids until the blood pressure rises on its own
Begin the prescribed 30 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid bolus
Give the prescribed as-needed antipyretic and recheck in 4 hours
items.rationale: Fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypotension and oliguria after abdominal surgery indicate sepsis, and the first-hour bundle is cultures, antibiotics and a 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus. Mean arterial pressure and hourly urine output show whether perfusion is being restored. Withholding fluids, treating only the fever, or handing monitoring back to assistive personnel every 4 hours all delay recognition; once a client is unstable, monitoring returns to the nurse.

items.stem: A charge nurse in a long-term care facility is planning care for a resident with moderate dementia who wanders during the afternoon. Which task is appropriate to delegate to assistive personnel?
options: Assessing the resident for causes of the increased afternoon agitation
Determining when the as-needed antianxiety medication should be given
Deciding whether the wandering requires a change in the resident's care plan
Escorting the resident on regular walks in the secured courtyard and reporting any agitation
items.rationale: Escorting a resident on a scheduled walk is a routine, predictable activity, and observing and reporting behavior is exactly what assistive personnel are expected to contribute. Changing the care plan, judging the need for an as-needed medication and searching for causes of agitation all require assessment and clinical judgment. The nurse uses the observations reported back to decide what the behavior means.

items.stem: A nurse cares for a client with right-sided weakness after a stroke who has been cleared by speech-language pathology for a regular diet. Which task may the nurse delegate to assistive personnel?
options: Checking the gag reflex before the first meal of the day
Setting up the meal tray within reach and staying with the client during the meal
Feeding a different client on the unit who coughs when drinking thin liquids
Deciding whether the diet texture can be advanced
items.rationale: Once swallowing has been evaluated and a regular diet ordered, meal setup and supervision are routine tasks for assistive personnel, who also report any coughing or pocketing of food. Feeding a client who coughs on thin liquids involves an unresolved aspiration risk, and testing a gag reflex or advancing a diet texture are assessment and planning decisions. Delegation depends on whether the client's response is predictable.

items.stem: A nurse is caring for a client whose ileostomy was created 2 days ago. Which part of this client's care must the nurse perform rather than delegate to assistive personnel?
options: Inspecting the stoma for color and viability and checking the peristomal skin
Measuring and recording the ostomy output
Emptying the ostomy pouch when it is one-third full
Assisting the client with a shower and hygiene
items.rationale: Inspecting a new stoma for a dusky or dark color and evaluating the surrounding skin is an assessment, and early ischemia must be recognized by a nurse. Emptying the pouch, recording output and assisting with hygiene are routine tasks that assistive personnel may perform while reporting anything unusual. A recent surgical site does not by itself make every related task nursing work; the judgment required does.

items.stem: A charge nurse on a behavioral health unit must arrange continuous observation for a client placed on suicide precautions. Which action is appropriate?
options: Assign trained assistive personnel to keep continuous visual observation and report any statement about self-harm immediately
Ask the client's visiting family member to stay in the room overnight instead of staff
Delegate the suicide risk reassessment to the assistive personnel providing the observation
Move the client to a quiet room at the end of the hall so the door can stay closed for privacy
items.rationale: Continuous visual observation is a structured, defined task that trained assistive personnel may carry out, with explicit direction to report any self-harm statement or behavior to the nurse at once. Reassessing suicide risk is an ongoing nursing assessment and cannot be delegated. Family members are not staff and cannot be given responsibility for safety, and isolating the client away from staff view increases risk rather than reducing it.

items.stem: A nurse on a pediatric unit is caring for a 2-year-old admitted with bronchiolitis. Which task may the nurse delegate to assistive personnel?
options: Teaching the parent how to use a bulb syringe at home
Performing nasopharyngeal suctioning before each feeding
Weighing the diapers and recording the results
Counting the respiratory rate and deciding whether the retractions have worsened
items.rationale: Weighing diapers is a standard measurement that assistive personnel are trained to perform and report, and it gives the nurse the output data needed for a small child. Judging whether retractions have worsened is respiratory assessment, suctioning requires evaluating work of breathing and tolerance, and parent teaching requires assessing understanding. Collecting a number may be delegated; interpreting it may not.

items.stem: A charge nurse on a postpartum unit is choosing an assignment for an LPN/LVN. Which client is most appropriate?
options: A client 2 hours after birth with a boggy uterus receiving an oxytocin infusion
A client 1 day after an uncomplicated vaginal birth who needs perineal care and scheduled analgesics
A client who needs the initial breastfeeding assessment and latch teaching
A client admitted with postpartum preeclampsia receiving magnesium sulfate
items.rationale: A client on the first postpartum day after an uncomplicated birth is stable with a predictable course, and perineal care and scheduled analgesics are within LPN/LVN practice. Uterine atony with an oxytocin infusion and magnesium sulfate therapy both require continuous registered nurse assessment for hemorrhage and toxicity. Initial breastfeeding assessment and teaching require evaluating latch, transfer and maternal knowledge, which is RN work.

items.stem: A nurse delegates 2-hour repositioning for a client on bed rest. Which action by the nurse demonstrates the right supervision and evaluation?
options: Asking the oncoming nurse to verify that the turns occurred
Reviewing the flow sheet only after the shift has ended
Checking the client's position and skin during rounds and asking the assistive personnel how the turning schedule is going
Assuming the turning was done because the assistive personnel is experienced
items.rationale: Supervision means monitoring the delegated task while there is still time to correct it, which is why the nurse looks at the client and talks with the assistive personnel during the shift. Experience does not replace follow-up, and reviewing documentation after the shift cannot prevent a pressure injury that has already begun. Handing verification to the next nurse passes along accountability that belongs to the delegating nurse.

items.stem: Assistive personnel offer, 'I can suction the client's tracheostomy while you finish the medication pass.' Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?
options: 'Ask the LPN/LVN to stand next to you while you do it.'
'Yes, go ahead, you have watched it done many times.'
'Only if you have done it before at another facility.'
'Thank you, but suctioning requires assessing breath sounds, so I will do it; please tell me if the client sounds congested.'
items.rationale: Suctioning an artificial airway requires assessing breath sounds, oxygenation and tolerance of the procedure, so it is outside the assistive personnel role regardless of how often it has been observed. The nurse declines clearly, explains why, and redirects the offer into something useful and within scope, which is reporting a change. Prior exposure at another facility and observation by an LPN/LVN do not expand a scope of practice set by the state.

items.stem: A charge nurse must build an assignment for a nurse floated from an outpatient surgery center to a medical-surgical unit. Which clients should the charge nurse avoid assigning to this nurse? Select all that apply.
options: A client receiving a heparin infusion titrated to activated partial thromboplastin time results
A client receiving the first dose of intravenous chemotherapy
A client with a tracheostomy placed yesterday who needs hourly suctioning
A client in alcohol withdrawal requiring CIWA scoring every 2 hours and intravenous lorazepam
A client with pneumonia on oral antibiotics who is awaiting discharge
A client with a healing pressure injury who needs a daily dressing change
items.rationale: Titrated anticoagulation, a new tracheostomy, hazardous drug administration and withdrawal scoring with intravenous sedation all require unit-specific competencies and rapid judgment that an outpatient surgery nurse is unlikely to have maintained. A routine dressing change and a stable client on oral antibiotics fall within general nursing practice. Matching assignment to demonstrated competence protects the client and does not insult the floated nurse.

items.stem: A home health registered nurse supervises an LPN/LVN who makes interim visits between the nurse's own visits. Which activities may the registered nurse assign to the LPN/LVN? Select all that apply.
options: Making the initial assessment visit for a newly referred client
Administering the client's scheduled intramuscular vitamin B12 injection
Revising the plan of care after the client's condition changes
Changing the dressing on a chronic venous ulcer following the established plan
Reinforcing the diet teaching the registered nurse started at the last visit
Obtaining a blood glucose reading and reporting values outside the stated range
items.rationale: Established wound care, scheduled intramuscular injections, ordered monitoring with defined report-back parameters, and reinforcement of teaching already begun are all within LPN/LVN home health practice. The initial assessment visit sets the plan of care and must be done by the registered nurse, who is also the only one who may revise that plan when the client changes. Working alone in a home does not expand what an LPN/LVN may legally do.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A nurse is assigning tasks to assistive personnel who joined the unit yesterday. Before delegating transfers with the mechanical lift, the nurse should {{1}}. If the nurse is unsure whether a task may be delegated at all, the nurse should consult {{2}}.

options: have another assistive personnel explain the lift during the first transfer
verify that the assistive personnel has been trained and checked off on that specific lift
ask whether the assistive personnel feels comfortable using lifts in general
assume the training was completed during hospital orientation
the assistive personnel's description of the previous employer's rules
the preference of the previous shift's charge nurse
the client's family about what they are willing to accept
the state nurse practice act and the facility's written job descriptions

items.rationale: The right person means the nurse confirms documented competence with the exact equipment before delegating, because comfort or general experience is not verification. When a task's status is unclear, the state nurse practice act and the employer's job descriptions define what may be delegated, not custom or convenience. Delegating without confirming training leaves both the client and the nurse's license exposed.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A preceptor sees the orientee preparing to give a scheduled dose of metoprolol to a client whose apical heart rate is 46 beats per minute. The preceptor should {{1}}, and once the client is safe should {{2}}.

options: allow the dose and discuss the hold parameters afterward
document the error in the orientation record before saying anything
stop the orientee before the dose is given and recheck the apical rate together
ask the charge nurse to speak with the orientee about it
review the hold parameters for beta blockers and the plan to notify the provider
report the orientee to the state board of nursing
complete an incident report without telling the orientee
move the orientee to clients without cardiac medications for the rest of orientation

items.rationale: Supervising a licensed orientee means intervening before harm occurs, so the preceptor stops the dose and verifies the apical rate, since metoprolol is held for bradycardia. Teaching follows immediately, connecting the parameter to the action and to provider notification, which is how judgment is built. Removing the orientee from all cardiac clients, silent documentation, or a board report are disproportionate responses to a single teachable moment caught before harm.

items.stem: A charge nurse drafts the assignment for the oncoming day shift. Click to highlight the assignments that must be changed before the shift begins.

highlightSegments.text: 0645 draft assignment for the day shift: 18 clients and five staff members.
Registered nurse A, 6 years on this unit: the client on a titrated nitroglycerin infusion and the client newly diagnosed with sepsis.
Registered nurse B, floated this morning from the outpatient endoscopy unit: both clients on continuous bladder irrigation after prostate surgery.
Registered nurse B also takes the client with cellulitis receiving intravenous antibiotics.
New graduate nurse in week 3 of orientation: the client in room 22 who is being actively resuscitated, with the preceptor unavailable until 1000.
LPN/LVN: scheduled medications and routine dressing changes for four stable clients.
LPN/LVN will also complete the admission assessment for the client transferring from the intensive care unit at 0900.
Assistive personnel: vital signs every 4 hours, hygiene and ambulation for the stable clients.
Assistive personnel will sit with the client on continuous observation and report any statement about self-harm.
Assistive personnel will decide whether the client in room 19 is stable enough to shower.

items.rationale: Continuous bladder irrigation demands a competency an endoscopy nurse is unlikely to hold, a resuscitation is far beyond a third-week orientee whose preceptor is unavailable, admission assessment is a registered nurse function, and judging whether a client is stable enough to shower is assessment rather than a delegable task. The remaining assignments match each person's license and demonstrated competence, which is what makes an assignment safe.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the LPN/LVN's midshift report that the registered nurse must assess personally before the plan of care continues unchanged.

highlightSegments.text: 1400 report from the LPN/LVN on an 86-year-old resident with dementia and atrial fibrillation.
Scheduled apixaban and metoprolol were given at 0900.
The apical heart rate taken before the metoprolol was 52 beats per minute.
The resident ate half of breakfast and all of a mid-morning snack.
A new bruise about 8 cm across is present over the left flank, and no fall was witnessed.
The resident walked to the dining room with a walker as usual.
The resident has been calling out for a spouse who died years ago, which is new today.
Blood pressure is 132/78 mm Hg and temperature is 36.8 C (98.2 F).
The incontinence brief was changed three times and the urine has a strong odor.
The family called to ask about the care conference scheduled for next week.

items.rationale: A beta blocker given at an apical rate of 52 needs the nurse to reassess the rate and review the hold parameters, and an unexplained large bruise in a resident on an anticoagulant raises concern for bleeding and an unwitnessed fall. New calling out for a deceased spouse together with strong-smelling urine suggests delirium from a urinary tract infection. Intake, a usual walk, stable vital signs and a family scheduling call need no urgent assessment.

items.stem: A charge nurse reviews the unit's data from the past three night shifts before making tonight's assignment. Which conclusion should the charge nurse draw?
options: The missed turns are a documentation problem and need only a chart audit
