items.stem: A client receiving hemodialysis who is being evaluated for kidney transplantation tells the nurse, 'I have missed four treatments this month and I stopped my phosphate binders because I cannot afford them.' Which action by the nurse best supports the evaluation?
options: Document the disclosure and notify the transplant coordinator so that the team can address the cost barrier and build an adherence plan
Advise the client not to mention this to the transplant team so that candidacy is not jeopardized
Recommend that the client withdraw from the evaluation until attendance has been consistent for six months
Reassure the client that dialysis attendance is not part of a transplant evaluation
items.rationale: Transplant evaluation is a team process in which adherence and the barriers behind it are assessed and treated, not hidden: a social worker and pharmacist can address medication cost, and missed treatments prompt a plan rather than automatic exclusion. Concealing the information from the team is dishonest and endangers a scarce organ. Telling the client attendance does not matter is inaccurate, and advising withdrawal removes the very support that could make the client a candidate.

items.stem: A nurse on an inpatient rehabilitation unit is preparing for the weekly interdisciplinary team conference for a client recovering from a stroke. Which actions by the nurse contribute to an effective conference? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the discussion to nursing problems so that the meeting finishes on time
Review the therapists' endurance and transfer findings before the meeting so the discussion builds on them
Ask the client and family beforehand which goals matter most to them and present those goals
Report the barriers identified on the home environment assessment, such as the stairs to the front door
Bring current data on functional progress, continence and skin integrity from the past week
Wait for the physician to set the goals and record them in the chart afterward
items.rationale: A rehabilitation conference works when each discipline arrives with current data and the team converts it into shared, measurable goals with a target discharge date. The nurse contributes around-the-clock information the therapists do not see, carries the client's and family's own priorities into the room, and raises environmental barriers early enough to solve them. Recording physician-set goals afterward makes the nurse a scribe, and confining the discussion to nursing problems defeats the purpose of the meeting.

items.stem: A nurse in a long-term care facility reviews the trended record for a resident during the minimum data set assessment period. Which conclusion should the nurse draw?
options: The findings should be recorded and left for the next quarterly review
The resident should be placed on a fluid restriction until meal intake improves
The weight change is an expected effect of aging and needs only monthly weights
A nutrition care area is triggered, and the interdisciplinary team must reassess the resident and revise the care plan
items.rationale: A loss of 5.1 kg is about 7.5 percent of body weight in a month, well past the 5 percent threshold that counts as significant, and it is accompanied by falling intake and a new need for feeding assistance. That combination triggers the nutrition care area, which obliges the interdisciplinary team to assess the cause and revise the care plan now, not at the next quarterly review. Calling it normal aging or restricting fluids ignores a measurable, treatable decline.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the home hospice visit note that require the nurse to arrange follow-up before leaving the home.

highlightSegments.text: 1400 Routine home visit for a client with metastatic pancreatic cancer, enrolled in hospice for six weeks.
Client rates abdominal pain 8 out of 10 and says the last breakthrough morphine dose was 'sometime yesterday.'
The spouse says, 'I am afraid of giving too much and killing him, so I hold off as long as I can.'
Four doses of concentrated oral morphine remain in the home.
Client is taking sips of water and eating very little, which the family understands is expected.
A hospital bed and a bedside commode are in the living room and both are in use.
Stage 2 sacral pressure injury unchanged since the last visit, dressing dry and intact.
Client states, 'I want to stay at home; I do not want to go back to the hospital.'
The spouse is the only caregiver and has slept no more than 2 hours a night for the past week.
The do-not-resuscitate order is posted on the refrigerator where it can be seen.
A daughter is arriving from out of state tomorrow to help with care.

items.rationale: Uncontrolled pain in hospice is an emergency of comfort, and here it has three linked causes the nurse can fix today: a caregiver who fears causing death by giving opioids, a supply about to run out, and exhaustion that makes reliable dosing impossible. The nurse teaches and reassures the spouse, arranges an urgent refill and requests respite or added aide hours. Declining intake, a stable pressure injury, the posted order and the preference to stay home are expected and already being managed.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client receiving home hospice care dies at 0300, and the spouse telephones the on-call hospice nurse. The nurse should {{1}}, and should explain that the hospice will offer the family {{2}} for at least 13 months after the death.

options: visit to verify the death according to agency policy, support the family, and dispose of the controlled substances with a witness
tell the spouse to call the funeral home and wait for the next scheduled visit
instruct the spouse to call 911 so that paramedics can attempt resuscitation
advise the spouse to take the body to the emergency department for a death certificate
a refund for the days of the hospice benefit that were not used
a home health aide to help with household chores
bereavement services such as counseling, support groups and scheduled follow-up contacts
daily nursing visits to the surviving spouse

items.rationale: An expected death at home is managed by the hospice, not by emergency services: the on-call nurse comes to the home, verifies the death, supports the family through the first hours, notifies the provider and funeral home, and destroys the remaining controlled substances with a witness as agency policy requires. Calling 911 invites unwanted resuscitation. Bereavement support is part of the hospice benefit and continues with the family for about a year after the death.

items.stem: A 7-year-old is sent to the school health office with a temperature of 39.1 C (102.4 F), a harsh cough, runny nose and red watery eyes for 3 days, and a blotchy red rash that began at the hairline and has spread down the face and neck. The parent confirms the child has received no immunizations. Complete the diagram by selecting the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess progress.
bowtieActions: Apply a topical antihistamine to the rash and document it as an allergic reaction
Send a classroom-wide message naming the child so families can watch for symptoms
Return the child to class with an ice pack until the end of the school day
Telephone the local health department to report a suspected case and begin identifying exposed contacts
Place the child alone in a room with the door closed, put a mask on the child and use airborne precautions until the child is collected
bowtieParams: Height and weight percentile at the next screening
Respiratory effort, hydration and oral intake
Temperature and the progression of the rash
items.rationale: Fever with cough, coryza and conjunctivitis followed by a rash that starts at the hairline and moves downward in an unimmunized child is measles, which spreads by the airborne route and is immediately reportable so contact tracing and post-exposure prophylaxis can begin. Scarlet fever produces a sandpaper rash with strawberry tongue, fifth disease a slapped-cheek rash, and varicella vesicles in crops. Monitoring targets the complications of measles, pneumonia and dehydration.

items.stem: A client is in the preoperative holding area for a right inguinal hernia repair. The nurse notes that the operative site has not been marked and the transporter has arrived to take the client to the operating room. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Ask the client to mark the correct side so that the client's own understanding is recorded
Ask the transporter to wait and notify the surgeon, who marks the site with the client participating before the client leaves the holding area
Confirm the side with the client and mark the right groin before the client leaves the holding area
Document that the correct side was verified verbally with the client and allow the transport to proceed
items.rationale: Site marking is done by the licensed practitioner who will perform the procedure, at or near the site, with the awake client taking part, and it must be done before the client leaves the preoperative area. The nurse's role in the Universal Protocol is to verify that the mark exists and matches the consent, and to stop the process when it does not. A mark made by the nurse or by the client, or a verbal check alone, does not satisfy the protocol and is a wrong-site surgery risk.

items.stem: A circulating nurse is transferring a client from the operating room to the post-anesthesia care unit at the end of a bowel resection. Place the steps in the correct order.
options: Inspect the dressing, drains and intravenous lines with the receiving nurse and answer any remaining questions before leaving
Confirm with the anesthesia provider that the client is stable enough to leave the operating room
Move the client onto the post-anesthesia care unit bed and apply the monitors and prescribed supplemental oxygen
Give the structured handoff report to the receiving post-anesthesia care unit nurse
Assess the airway, breathing and circulation on arrival together with the anesthesia provider
items.rationale: A client leaves the operating room only when the anesthesia provider judges the airway and circulation stable for transport. On arrival the first priority is restoring monitoring and oxygen, then an immediate airway, breathing and circulation assessment, because those are the parameters that change fastest during emergence. The verbal handoff follows, and the two nurses then examine the dressing, drains and lines together so the receiving nurse has a baseline before responsibility passes.

items.stem: A charge nurse on a labor and delivery unit reviews the assignments made for the oncoming shift. Which assignment requires revision?
options: One nurse assigned to a client in the second stage of labor pushing with epidural analgesia
One nurse assigned to two clients in early latent labor who are not receiving oxytocin
One nurse assigned to a stable couplet 2 hours after an uncomplicated vaginal birth
One nurse assigned to a client in active labor receiving an oxytocin infusion and to a second client in early labor
items.rationale: Oxytocin is a high-alert medication that requires continuous evaluation of contraction pattern and fetal heart rate with titration at the bedside, so a client receiving it in active labor is a one-to-one assignment and cannot be paired with another laboring client. One-to-one care is also the standard during the second stage. Two clients in latent labor without oxytocin, or a stable mother-newborn couplet, are within accepted perinatal staffing ratios.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: Before a newborn is taken from the mother's room for a hearing screen, the nurse must {{1}}. If a newborn's security tag alarms at a unit exit door, the staff member nearest that door should {{2}}.

options: read the newborn's name from the crib card
verify that the newborn has fed within the past hour
match the numbers on the newborn's and the mother's identification bands and scan the newborn's band
ask the mother to state the newborn's date of birth
assume the tag is loose and ask the parents to reapply it
silence the alarm and continue with the assigned care
remain at the door, prevent anyone from passing through it and call the abduction alert
document the alarm and report it at the end of the shift

items.rationale: Matching band numbers between the newborn and the mother at every separation and reunion is what prevents an infant being handed to the wrong family, and band scanning creates a record of each transfer. A security tag alarm is treated as a possible abduction until proved otherwise, so the exit is covered first and the alert is called; silencing the alarm, assuming a loose tag or documenting it later all allow an infant to leave the secured unit while staff investigate.

items.stem: A 4-year-old with a developmental delay is admitted for a scheduled tonsillectomy, and the parents speak only Spanish. Which actions should the nurse take to coordinate the child's perioperative care? Select all that apply.
options: Include the child's developmental level and usual way of communicating in the handoff to the operating room nurse
Arrange a qualified medical interpreter for the preoperative teaching and the consent discussion
Give the preoperative teaching in English and hand the parents a Spanish pamphlet at discharge
Ask the child's 10-year-old cousin to interpret the preoperative instructions for the parents
Arrange for one parent to remain with the child until induction of anesthesia if facility policy allows
Send the parents to the cafeteria before transport so that the child settles more quickly
Ask the parents which comfort items and routines help the child cope and pass that information to the perioperative team
items.rationale: Coordinating a child's surgery means carrying the family's knowledge of the child into an unfamiliar setting: a professional interpreter makes teaching and consent valid, the parents' comfort strategies and the child's communication method belong in the handoff, and parental presence at induction reduces distress. A child relative must never interpret, because accuracy and confidentiality cannot be assured. Teaching in a language the family does not read leaves them unable to give care at home.

items.stem: An 8-year-old is returning to school after hospitalization for a new diagnosis of type 1 diabetes. Which actions should the nurse include when coordinating the return to school? Select all that apply.
options: Obtain the family's written authorization before health information is shared with teachers
Obtain the provider orders for insulin dosing, glucose monitoring and hypoglycemia treatment during the school day
Develop an individualized school health plan with the family and the school nurse
Plan for glucose checks and snacks in the classroom so the child is not sent out of class for every check
Arrange training for the staff who supervise the child at lunch, in physical education and on field trips
Ask the classroom teacher to keep the child's insulin in an unlocked desk drawer for convenience
Advise the family to keep the child at home until the glucose readings have been stable for a month
items.rationale: School re-entry after a chronic illness diagnosis succeeds when the medical plan becomes a school plan: written orders, an individualized health plan, trained staff for every part of the school day, and family authorization for the information teachers need. Allowing monitoring in the classroom keeps the child in class and normalizes the routine. Keeping a healthy child home delays adjustment and learning, and insulin stored unsecured in a classroom is a medication safety hazard.

items.stem: Click to highlight the findings in the transition clinic note that show the adolescent is not yet ready to transfer to adult care.

highlightSegments.text: 1030 Transition clinic visit for a 17-year-old with sickle cell disease followed in this clinic since infancy.
The parent books all of the appointments and telephones for every prescription refill.
The client names hydroxyurea and the dose taken each morning without prompting.
The client says, 'I do not know what I am supposed to do if a pain crisis starts when I am away at college.'
An adult hematologist has been identified, but the client has not met them and no first appointment is scheduled.
The client carries a wallet card listing the diagnosis, the usual crisis plan and the clinic telephone number.
The client states they have never spoken with a clinician without a parent in the room.
The client drives to appointments and works part time at a grocery store.
The client is unsure whether the current health insurance continues after the 18th birthday.
Hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, which is this client's stated baseline.
The client plans to start community college in the autumn and lives at home.

items.rationale: Transition readiness is measured by self-management skills, not by age or by how stable the disease is: knowing the crisis plan, managing refills and appointments, being able to speak with a clinician alone, having an adult provider who has actually met the client, and understanding insurance continuity. Those gaps are all addressed before transfer. Naming the medication, carrying a summary card, working and driving show existing strengths that the plan can build on.

items.stem: A client brought to the emergency department by police is placed on a 72-hour emergency psychiatric hold after threatening suicide. Two hours later the client says, 'I have changed my mind, I am leaving now,' and walks toward the exit. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Apply four-point restraints so that the client remains in the treatment area
Allow the client to leave and document that the client refused treatment
Tell the client that leaving will result in arrest by the police who brought them in
Calmly tell the client that the hold requires a psychiatric evaluation before discharge, stay with the client and notify the provider and security as needed
items.rationale: An emergency hold is a legal authorization to detain a client for evaluation, so the client may not leave, but detention is maintained with the least restrictive measure that works: presence, calm explanation and staff support, escalating only if behavior makes the client or others unsafe. Restraint is an intervention for imminent danger with its own order and monitoring requirements, not a way to enforce a hold. Letting the client go ignores the order, and threatening arrest is coercive.

items.stem: A nurse is working on an inpatient behavioral health unit. For each nursing action, indicate whether it supports or undermines the therapeutic milieu.
matrixRows: Hold a daily community meeting at which clients set goals and raise concerns about the unit
Make an exception to the unit schedule for the client who complains most loudly
Apply the unit rules consistently to every client and explain the reason behind each rule
Answer another client's question about a client's diagnosis so that the unit feels open
Assign staff to remain visible and available in the day room rather than behind the nurses' station
Invite clients to help plan the weekend activity schedule
items.rationale: The milieu is itself a treatment: predictable structure, consistent limits, visible staff and shared decision making give clients a safe environment in which to practice new behavior. Inconsistent limits teach clients that rules are negotiable through pressure and set staff against each other, and disclosing one client's diagnosis to another breaks confidentiality and destroys the trust the milieu depends on.

items.stem: A client has finished adjuvant chemotherapy for stage II breast cancer and is being transitioned out of active treatment. Which action by the oncology nurse best coordinates the client's survivorship care?
options: Refer the client to hospice so that symptoms continue to be monitored
Schedule positron emission tomography scans every 3 months for the next 2 years
Explain that follow-up is no longer necessary unless new symptoms appear
Provide a written survivorship care plan listing the treatments received, the surveillance schedule and the late effects to watch for, and send a copy to the primary care provider
items.rationale: Survivorship care transfers ownership of follow-up from the cancer center to the client and the primary care provider, and it only works if both receive the same written summary: what was given, what surveillance is due and when, and which late effects, such as cardiotoxicity or a second cancer, to watch for. Routine interval imaging is not recommended for asymptomatic survivors, stopping follow-up abandons surveillance, and hospice is for clients no longer pursuing disease-directed treatment.

items.stem: A client receiving chemotherapy telephones the oncology clinic on day 12 of the cycle. The nurse reviews the trended data. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Arrange immediate evaluation so that blood cultures are drawn and broad-spectrum antibiotics are started within 1 hour
Tell the client to recheck the temperature in 4 hours and call back if it remains above 38 C
Instruct the client to go to the emergency department and wait in the general waiting area to be triaged
Advise the client to continue acetaminophen and keep the appointment scheduled in 2 days
trendRows: Mild sore throat and chills overnight
Shaking chills this morning, took acetaminophen
items.rationale: An absolute neutrophil count below 500 with a temperature of 38.5 C is neutropenic fever, an oncologic emergency in which every hour of delay to antibiotics increases mortality; cultures are drawn and empiric antibiotics given within an hour. Antipyretics mask the only reliable sign of infection in a client who cannot mount inflammation. Waiting 2 days or rechecking later wastes that window, and sitting in a crowded waiting area exposes a profoundly neutropenic client to further pathogens.

items.stem: A client who receives hemodialysis on Monday, Wednesday and Friday is admitted to a medical unit on a Tuesday with pneumonia. Which actions should the admitting nurse take to coordinate the client's dialysis care? Select all that apply.
options: Notify nephrology of the admission so that inpatient treatments are scheduled
Contact the outpatient dialysis unit for the treatment schedule, the dry weight and the access history
Communicate the fluid restriction to the team and record intake and output every shift
Arrange for meal trays to be delivered during the dialysis treatment so that no meal is missed
Cancel the Wednesday treatment because the client is receiving intravenous antibiotics
Clarify with the provider and pharmacist which medications should be held until after dialysis
Weigh the client on admission and each morning before breakfast on the same scale
items.rationale: An admitted dialysis client keeps an outpatient prescription that the inpatient team has to reconstruct: schedule, dry weight, access and fluid limits all come from the dialysis unit, and nephrology must be told at once so no treatment is missed. Daily standardized weights are how fluid status is judged between treatments, and dialyzable medications are timed around it. Intravenous antibiotics are a reason to coordinate dosing, not to omit dialysis; eating during treatment risks hypotension.

items.stem: A client is scheduled for discharge tomorrow after kidney transplantation. The nurse learns that the insurer has not authorized tacrolimus and the client has no supply at home. Which action by the nurse is most appropriate?
options: Discharge the client with the written prescription and instruct them to telephone the insurer in the morning
Instruct the client to take half of the prescribed dose until the authorization is approved
Notify the transplant coordinator, the transplant pharmacist and the social worker so that a supply is secured before the client leaves
Send the client home with medication returned to the unit by another transplant client
items.rationale: Even a short gap in a calcineurin inhibitor after transplantation risks acute rejection and graft loss, so discharge does not happen until the medication is physically in the client's hands; the coordinator, transplant pharmacist and social worker have the authorization, assistance program and starter supply pathways to solve it. Halving the dose produces subtherapeutic levels, and dispensing medication returned by another client is unsafe and outside any nurse's authority.

items.stem: A nurse is coordinating discharge home from an inpatient rehabilitation unit for a client recovering from a spinal cord injury. Place the steps in the correct order.
options: Provide hands-on caregiver training on the equipment the client will use and document a return demonstration
Confirm on the day of discharge that the equipment has been delivered and the first home visit is scheduled
Arrange the durable medical equipment, home care services and follow-up appointments the team identified
Complete the interdisciplinary discharge readiness review of function, equipment needs and caregiver ability
Conduct the home environment assessment with the therapy team and the family
items.rationale: Rehabilitation discharge planning moves from assessment to arrangement to verification. The team first agrees on what the client can do and what support is missing, the home visit shows which of those needs the physical environment creates, and only then can the right equipment and services be ordered. Caregivers are trained on the equipment that has actually been chosen, and the plan is confirmed on the day of discharge so the client does not arrive home to an empty house.

items.stem: The resident council of a long-term care facility tells the director of nursing that evening meals arrive cold and that call lights on the east wing often go unanswered for more than 20 minutes. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Explain to the council that meal service and staffing levels are decided by the corporate office
Suggest that families bring meals from home and answer call lights when they are visiting
Ask residents to bring concerns to their own nurse individually rather than through the council
Acknowledge the concerns, investigate them with the dietary and nursing teams, and give the council a written response stating the actions taken and the timeline
items.rationale: Residents have the right to organize a council, and the facility is required to listen to its grievances and respond, which means investigating the concerns with the responsible departments and reporting back what will change and by when. Deflecting to corporate, redirecting residents to individual complaints or shifting the work to families dismisses a formal grievance, and unanswered call lights are also a safety issue that the facility must act on.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client with metastatic lung cancer receiving home hospice care has dyspnea at rest despite scheduled sustained-release morphine. The visiting nurse should {{1}}, and should contact the hospice provider to request {{2}}.

options: withhold further opioid because of the risk of respiratory depression
arrange transport to the emergency department for evaluation
position the client upright, direct a fan toward the face and give the prescribed breakthrough dose
lower the head of the bed and coach the client through deep breathing exercises
an increase in the breakthrough opioid dose, with a low-dose anxiolytic if anxiety is adding to the dyspnea
a course of intravenous antibiotics to be started in the home
an order to stop the morphine and use oxygen alone
a referral for outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation

items.rationale: Opioids are the first-line treatment for the sensation of breathlessness at the end of life, and airflow across the face from a fan plus an upright position relieves dyspnea within minutes while the dose takes effect. Escalating the dose for uncontrolled symptoms is appropriate in hospice and does not hasten death. Withholding the opioid, transporting the client against the plan of care, or substituting oxygen alone leaves a treatable, frightening symptom untreated.

items.stem: A client with end-stage heart failure enrolled in home hospice, with a do-not-resuscitate order in place, tells the nurse that the implantable cardioverter-defibrillator has delivered two painful shocks in the past week. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Reassure the client that the shocks show the device is working as intended
Explain that the defibrillator must remain active because it was implanted before the client enrolled in hospice
Contact the hospice provider to arrange deactivation of the defibrillator function in keeping with the client's goals of care
Place a magnet over the device and tape it in place until the next scheduled visit
items.rationale: A do-not-resuscitate order does not switch off an implanted defibrillator; deactivation requires its own discussion, order and reprogramming by a device technician, and the pacing function can be left on for comfort. Shocks at the end of life cause pain and distress without changing the outcome, which is exactly the conflict between the device and the goals of care that the hospice team must resolve. A taped magnet is an emergency measure, not a plan, and it fails as soon as it shifts.

items.stem: An occupational health nurse receives a note from the provider of an employee recovering from a back injury that reads 'modified duty, no lifting over 4.5 kg (10 lb) for 4 weeks.' Which action by the nurse is most appropriate?
options: Return the employee to full duty and rely on them to avoid lifting anything heavy
Tell the employee to stay off work until the provider releases them with no restrictions at all
Send the supervisor a copy of the medical record so that the restrictions are understood in context
Meet with the employee and the supervisor to match the written restrictions to available modified duty, and document the plan and the review date
items.rationale: Return-to-work coordination translates clinical restrictions into specific tasks the employee may do, agreed with the supervisor and written down with a date to review, which is what keeps the worker safe and employed. The supervisor is entitled to the restrictions and capabilities only; the diagnosis and medical record stay confidential in occupational health. Keeping a worker off entirely delays recovery, and relying on the employee to self-limit puts the injury and the employer's obligation at risk.

items.stem: Click to highlight the entries in the telephone triage record that must be corrected or completed before the nurse closes the call record.

highlightSegments.text: 2145 Telephone call received from the parent of an 8-year-old with fever.
The caller's name is recorded, but no call-back telephone number is documented.
The child's date of birth and medical record number were verified with the caller.
Reported temperature 38.9 C (102.0 F) taken orally 30 minutes before the call.
The nurse asked about breathing, fluid intake, urine output and how easily the child could be roused.
Under advice given, the record reads only, 'Gave the parent some suggestions.'
The triage protocol used to guide the call is not named anywhere in the record.
The parent was told to call back or seek care immediately if the child becomes difficult to wake.
There is no entry showing that the caller understood the plan and agreed to follow it.
The time the call began is documented, but not the time it ended.
The entry is signed with the nurse's name and credentials.

items.rationale: A telephone triage record is the only evidence of an encounter with a client the nurse never saw, so it must show how the decision was reached and that it reached the caller: the protocol used, the specific advice given, the caller's understanding and agreement, a call-back number if the call is cut off, and the start and end times. Verified identifiers, the symptom questions asked, the stated red-flag instructions and the signature already meet the standard.

items.stem: A school nurse reviews the health office record for a 10-year-old student with asthma. Based on the trended data, which action should the nurse take?
options: Continue the current plan because the student is still attending school on most days
Teach the student to take the rescue inhaler before every class as a preventive measure
Contact the family and the primary care provider with the pattern and arrange an updated asthma action plan and staff training
Excuse the student from physical education until the peak flow returns to the personal best
trendHeaders: Rescue inhaler doses given in the health office
items.rationale: Rising rescue inhaler use, a peak flow falling into the yellow zone, night cough and lost school days together show worsening control that needs a change in the treatment plan, not tighter monitoring at school; the nurse reports the objective pattern to the family and provider and updates the action plan and the staff who follow it. Removing the student from physical education treats activity as the problem, and scheduled rescue inhaler use substitutes for the controller therapy the child actually needs.

items.stem: A surgical unit nurse receives a client transferred from the post-anesthesia care unit after a total hip arthroplasty. Which action should the nurse take first after the client is settled in the bed?
options: Complete the admission paperwork and transcribe the postoperative orders
Assess the airway, vital signs, pain, dressing, drains and intravenous access, and compare the findings with the report received
Ask assistive personnel to obtain vital signs while the nurse reviews the operative record
Allow the client to rest undisturbed and assess at the end of the hour
items.rationale: Accountability for the client passes at the moment of transfer, so the receiving nurse establishes a personal baseline immediately and checks it against what was reported; a discrepancy between the two is the earliest sign of bleeding, respiratory depression or an unrecognized complication. Orders and paperwork follow the assessment. Delegating the first set of vital signs after a transfer of care leaves the nurse without direct assessment data at the point where deterioration is most likely.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: During the preoperative interview for an elective open hernia repair, a client states that they took their usual apixaban dose 2 hours ago because 'nobody told me to stop it.' The nurse should {{1}}, and should recognize that this finding matters because {{2}}.

options: notify the surgeon and the anesthesia provider before the client is prepared any further
reassure the client that the effect will have worn off by the time of the incision
administer activated charcoal to reduce absorption of the dose
document the dose and continue with the preoperative checklist
a urinary catheter will now be required before the procedure
the surgical consent will have to be signed a second time
the anticoagulant raises the risk of intraoperative bleeding and can make neuraxial anesthesia unsafe
a new history and physical examination will have to be completed

items.rationale: Preoperative verification includes reconciling what the client actually took against the instructions given, because a direct oral anticoagulant taken hours before surgery raises bleeding risk and is a contraindication to spinal or epidural placement within the drug's holding window, with a risk of spinal hematoma. The decision to delay or proceed belongs to the surgeon and anesthesia provider, so the nurse escalates rather than absorbing the finding into the checklist.

items.stem: A client at 34 weeks of gestation comes to the emergency department of a hospital that has an obstetric unit, reporting decreased fetal movement since the previous evening. The registration clerk asks the charge nurse whether the client should simply be told to telephone the prenatal clinic. Which response by the charge nurse is correct?
options: 'Bring the client back now. She is entitled to a medical screening examination, which for a pregnant client includes fetal assessment, before any decision is made about where care continues.'
'Tell the client to call the clinic; the obstetric unit only evaluates clients who are in labor.'
'She can be sent home if she can feel the baby move at all while she is standing at the desk.'
'Have her wait in the lobby until her insurance and prenatal records are verified, then we will decide.'
items.rationale: Anyone who presents to a hospital emergency department must receive a medical screening examination before being redirected elsewhere, and for a pregnant client that screening includes assessment of the fetus and of whether labor is present. Decreased fetal movement is exactly the complaint that requires monitoring rather than a telephone triage. Verifying insurance before screening, or accepting a single movement as reassurance, delays the evaluation of fetal wellbeing.

items.stem: Click to highlight the items in the mother-newborn handoff report that require the oncoming nurse to follow up immediately.

highlightSegments.text: 1900 Handoff for a couplet on postpartum day 1 after a vaginal birth at 39 weeks.
Fundus firm at the umbilicus, lochia rubra, moderate on one pad over the past 4 hours.
Mother is O negative and the newborn is A positive; Rh immune globulin has not been given and no order appears on the chart.
Mother rates afterpains 3 out of 10 following scheduled ibuprofen.
Mother has voided twice since the epidural infusion was stopped.
Newborn axillary temperature was 36.2 C (97.2 F) at 1800; skin-to-skin was started and the temperature has not been rechecked.
The number on the newborn's identification band does not match the number on the mother's band.
Newborn has breastfed four times with two wet diapers and one stool.
Mother states, 'I have not been able to stop crying since this morning and I am scared to be alone with the baby.'
Hepatitis B vaccine given at 1200 with documented parental consent.
Discharge teaching is scheduled for tomorrow morning.

items.rationale: Rh immune globulin must be given within 72 hours to an Rh-negative mother with an Rh-positive newborn, and a missing order is a time-limited omission. A low newborn temperature that was never rechecked leaves cold stress unverified, and mismatched identification bands must be corrected at once. A statement of fear about being alone with the newborn calls for immediate mood and safety assessment. Firm fundus, controlled pain, voiding and feeding are expected first-day findings.

items.stem: An infant who requires gastrostomy feedings and an apnea monitor is being prepared for discharge home. For each action, indicate whether it must be completed before discharge or may be arranged after discharge.
matrixRows: The caregivers independently perform a gastrostomy feeding and demonstrate care of the site
The home equipment supplier delivers the feeding pump, monitor and supplies and confirms they work in the home
The caregivers complete infant cardiopulmonary resuscitation training
The infant's first early intervention developmental evaluation is completed
The electric utility company is notified that the home has life-sustaining equipment
The family's application to a respite care program is approved
items.rationale: Technology-dependent infants go home only when the home can support them: caregivers who can feed and resuscitate the infant without prompting, equipment that is present and working, and a utility company that knows to prioritize the address during an outage. Those cannot be finished later because failure of any one of them is life-threatening on the first night. Developmental evaluation and respite funding improve long-term outcomes but can be arranged in the weeks after the infant is safely home.

items.stem: A staff member who is providing continuous one-to-one observation for a client on suicide precautions tells the charge nurse they need to take a meal break. Which action should the charge nurse take?
options: Assign a trained replacement who takes over at the bedside and receives a handoff before the first observer leaves
Ask the client's roommate to alert staff if anything happens while the observer is away
Allow the observer to step out briefly once the client has fallen asleep
Have the client sit at the nurses' station where several staff can see them during the break
items.rationale: Continuous observation means the client is never unobserved, so the assignment is transferred person to person at the bedside with a handoff of the client's status, precautions and any recent statements, exactly like any other transfer of responsibility. Sleep does not reduce risk, general visibility at a busy station is not one-to-one observation, and no client or visitor can be given responsibility for another client's safety.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client is being discharged after an inpatient admission for a suicide attempt using a firearm kept at home. Before the client leaves the unit the nurse completes a safety plan that includes {{1}}, and confirms that {{2}}.

options: a written list of reasons the client should not feel depressed
a daily activity schedule written for the client by the nurse
a signed promise from the client not to attempt suicide again
the client's own warning signs, coping strategies and the specific people and crisis numbers to contact
the client has agreed to stay away from work until all symptoms resolve
the client's employer has been told about the admission
the firearm has been removed from the home by a named person and a follow-up appointment is scheduled within a week
the client has been given a 90-day supply of the prescribed antidepressant

items.rationale: A safety plan is written with the client: the warning signs they recognize, strategies that have worked, and named people and numbers to call, which is why a plan the nurse writes for the client does not work. Reducing access to the method used is the most effective step after a firearm attempt, and risk is highest in the first days after discharge, so follow-up is arranged within about a week. A no-suicide contract has no evidence of benefit and a large medication supply adds a method.

items.stem: A client on a locked inpatient behavioral health unit is placed on elopement precautions after twice being found at the stairwell door. Which actions should the nurse include in the plan? Select all that apply.
options: Explore with the client and the team what prompted the attempts and address the client's stated reasons
Assign the client to the room closest to the exit so that staff can see them pass by
Ensure staff accompany the client whenever they leave the unit for tests or activities
Prohibit all visitors so that the client is not tempted to leave with them
Place a current photograph of the client in the record so that staff can identify the client quickly if needed
State the elopement risk at every shift handoff and to any staff escorting the client off the unit
Account for the client visually at the assigned observation interval and document each check
items.rationale: Elopement precautions work through communication and presence: everyone involved in the client's care knows the risk, the client is accounted for on a set interval and escorted off the unit, and a current photograph makes a search effective. Addressing the reason behind the attempts, such as worry about a pet at home, treats the cause. Blanket visitor restriction removes support, and a room near the exit shortens the distance to an unsupervised door.

items.stem: A client is starting oral capecitabine at home after discharge from the oncology unit. Which action by the nurse best applies chemotherapy safety standards to the oral route?
options: Instruct the client to crush the tablets if swallowing becomes difficult
Treat the drug as a routine oral medication, because the client is taking tablets at home
Verify the regimen, dose and cycle days against the treatment plan with a second nurse, teach handling, storage and disposal precautions, and confirm the client knows which toxicities require a call
Instruct the client to take the tablets continuously until the next clinic visit
items.rationale: An oral antineoplastic is the same high-alert drug as an infusion, so the independent verification, the cycle schedule and the hazardous-handling precautions all still apply, and the client becomes the person administering it. Capecitabine is given on defined days with a rest period, and taking it continuously produces severe toxicity. The tablets must not be crushed, and diarrhea, mouth sores and hand-foot changes mean stopping and calling the clinic.

items.stem: A client in an outpatient infusion center is 12 minutes into a first dose of intravenous rituximab when they report itching, a tight throat and low back pain. Blood pressure has fallen from 128/76 to 92/54 mm Hg, heart rate is 118/min, and the face and chest are flushed. Complete the diagram by selecting the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess progress.
bowtieConditions: Vasovagal response to the needle insertion
bowtieActions: Stay with the client, call for help and give the prescribed emergency medications such as epinephrine, an antihistamine and a corticosteroid
Apply a cold compress over the intravenous site and elevate the arm
Stop the rituximab infusion at once and keep the line open with normal saline
Remove the intravenous catheter and restart it in the opposite arm
Slow the infusion to half the rate and continue while observing the client
bowtieParams: Serum uric acid and phosphate in 24 hours
Weight at the next clinic visit
items.rationale: Itching, throat tightness, flushing, back pain and hypotension minutes into a first monoclonal antibody dose are an infusion-related hypersensitivity reaction, which can progress to anaphylaxis. The infusion stops immediately while venous access is preserved with saline for emergency drugs, and the nurse stays with the client and calls for help. A vasovagal episode causes bradycardia, extravasation local swelling without systemic signs, and tumor lysis laboratory changes a day or more later.

items.stem: A client who performs four continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis exchanges a day at home is admitted to a medical unit with cellulitis of the arm. The unit nurses have not cared for a client on peritoneal dialysis before. Which action by the charge nurse best coordinates this client's care?
options: Contact the nephrology team and the peritoneal dialysis nurse to confirm the prescription and arrange staff support, and involve the client, who performs the exchanges independently, in the plan
Arrange for the client to be converted to hemodialysis for the duration of the admission
Hold the exchanges until discharge, since the admission is expected to be short
Ask a family member to come in and perform all of the exchanges during the admission
items.rationale: Peritoneal dialysis continues during hospitalization on the client's own prescription, and the safe way to cover a skill the unit lacks is to bring in the expertise rather than to omit the therapy: nephrology confirms the prescription and the dialysis nurse supports or performs the exchanges. A client who does the exchanges at home is a resource and should continue when able. Missing exchanges causes fluid overload and uremia, and converting to hemodialysis is a medical decision.

items.stem: Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
items.clozeText: A client who received a liver transplant 6 months ago is admitted to a community hospital with pneumonia. The nurse should {{1}}, and should notify {{2}} of the admission so that immunosuppression is managed correctly.

options: have the client bring in their own medications and self-administer them without reconciliation
hold the immunosuppressants until the infection has resolved
verify and continue the immunosuppressant regimen at the exact doses and times and check the new antibiotics for interactions
double the immunosuppressant dose because of the physiological stress of the infection
the operating surgeon, and only if the graft appears to be failing
the client's employer and insurance case manager only
the transplant center team that follows the client
the organ procurement organization that recovered the graft

items.rationale: Immunosuppressants are time-critical: even one missed or late dose of a calcineurin inhibitor risks rejection, and many antibiotics and antifungals alter tacrolimus levels dramatically, so reconciliation and interaction checking are part of the admission. Doses are changed only by the transplant team, which is why that team is notified of any admission and guides the balance between treating the infection and protecting the graft. The procurement organization has no role after transplantation.

items.stem: A nurse on an inpatient rehabilitation unit reviews the trended record for a client 3 weeks after surgical repair of a hip fracture. Which conclusion should the nurse bring to the interdisciplinary team conference?
options: Therapy should be increased to four sessions a day to push the client through the plateau
The client is progressing as expected and the current plan should continue unchanged
Progress has stalled and the team should reassess the pain management plan before revising the rehabilitation goals
The client is ready for discharge home now that transfers need only one person
items.rationale: Walking distance and transfers improved while pain was controlled and then flattened the week pain rose to 8 out of 10 and the client could complete only one session a day, so the limiting factor is a treatable symptom rather than a fixed ceiling on function. The team addresses analgesia timed before therapy first and then judges the goals. Adding sessions to a client who cannot tolerate the current schedule worsens pain, and one-person assist transfers alone do not make a client safe at home.

items.stem: A nurse in a skilled nursing facility is arranging the quarterly care plan conference for a resident who is alert and makes their own decisions. Which action is correct?
options: Invite the resident's adult child instead, because family members usually understand the plan better
Hold the conference with staff only and give the resident a copy of the finished care plan afterward
Invite the resident, and any representative the resident chooses, to attend and take part in setting the goals
Schedule the conference during the resident's therapy session so that the resident is not disturbed
items.rationale: A resident has the right to participate in planning their own care, so the conference is scheduled at a time the resident can attend, with anyone they choose to include, and the goals are written with them rather than for them. Substituting a family member for a decisional resident removes that right, handing over a completed plan makes participation meaningless, and deliberately scheduling around the resident guarantees they cannot attend.

items.stem: Click to highlight the entries in the palliative care note that show the current plan of care conflicts with the client's documented goals.

highlightSegments.text: 1500 Palliative care follow-up for a client with end-stage pulmonary fibrosis, hospital day 4.
The documented goals of care are comfort, discharge home, and no return to the intensive care unit.
The advance directive on the chart specifies do not resuscitate and do not intubate.
A bronchoscopy for tissue diagnosis is scheduled for tomorrow morning.
Orders include a 1,500 mL fluid restriction with a daily laboratory draw at 0400.
Morphine 2 mg intravenously every 2 hours as needed for dyspnea is ordered and has relieved the client's breathlessness.
A referral to home hospice was entered yesterday and accepted this morning.
The client was moved overnight to a telemetry bed for continuous cardiac monitoring.
Vital signs are being taken every 2 hours through the night.
Client states, 'I just want to be at home with my dog.'
The spouse says the family understands and supports the plan for hospice at home.
Oxygen at 4 L by nasal cannula, titrated for comfort.

items.rationale: When the goal is comfort and discharge home, every order should be tested against it: an invasive diagnostic bronchoscopy, predawn laboratory draws, telemetry monitoring that cannot be acted on under a do-not-intubate order, and overnight vital signs all disturb the client without changing the plan, and each should be discussed for discontinuation. The opioid for dyspnea, comfort-titrated oxygen and the hospice referral are consistent with the stated goals and are continued.

items.stem: A home hospice client's pain has been uncontrolled for 48 hours despite two dose adjustments, and the family is exhausted and frightened by the client's distress. Which action by the hospice nurse is most appropriate?
options: Increase the visit schedule to twice a week and reassess the pain at the next visit
Explain that the client must revoke the hospice benefit in order to receive any further treatment
Contact the hospice provider to arrange a change to continuous home care or a general inpatient level of care so the symptom crisis can be managed
Advise the family to call 911 so that the client can be admitted through the emergency department
items.rationale: Hospice includes higher levels of care for exactly this situation: continuous nursing in the home or a short inpatient admission to bring a symptom crisis under control, after which the client returns to routine home care. The benefit does not have to be revoked to obtain it, and an emergency department visit exposes the client to interventions that conflict with the plan of care. Waiting for the next routine visit leaves severe pain untreated and risks the family abandoning the plan to stay home.

items.stem: A community health nurse is coordinating care for a client newly diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis who lives with three household contacts. For each action, indicate whether it is indicated or not indicated.
matrixRows: Report the confirmed case to the local health department
Arrange testing and evaluation of the three household contacts
Wait until the client finishes treatment before notifying public health
Arrange directly observed therapy for the client's medication doses
Tell the client to stop the medications once the cough has resolved
Teach the client to wear a mask when others are in the home and during transport until cleared as noninfectious
items.rationale: Active tuberculosis is a reportable disease, and the report is what starts the contact investigation that finds infection in the household before it becomes disease, so it is made at diagnosis rather than at the end of treatment. Directly observed therapy is standard because months of multidrug treatment are difficult to complete and interrupted therapy breeds resistance. Symptoms improve long before the client is cured, so stopping when the cough clears is the classic route to drug-resistant disease.

items.stem: A nurse in a telehealth call center answers a call from a client reporting new abdominal pain. Place the steps in the correct order.
options: Ask the caller to describe the problem in their own words and determine whether it is an emergency
Document the protocol used, the advice given, the disposition and the caller's agreement with the plan
Verify the caller's identity, the client's identifiers and a call-back telephone number
State the disposition and the specific warning signs that mean the caller should seek care sooner
Work through the symptom-specific triage protocol for abdominal pain
items.rationale: Identifiers and a call-back number come first so that the nurse is advising the right person and can reach them if the call drops, which happens most often in the calls that turn out to be emergencies. An open description then screens for a condition that needs 911 before any protocol is worked through. The protocol produces a disposition, the caller is told what would change that disposition, and the record is completed while the details are accurate.

items.stem: An occupational health nurse is coordinating the response after an employee sustains a needlestick from a device used on a client whose bloodborne pathogen status is unknown. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
options: Ensure that post-exposure prophylaxis is started within hours when it is indicated
Tell the employee's unit manager the source client's name and diagnosis
Obtain the employee's baseline serology
Arrange the follow-up testing and counseling at the intervals the protocol specifies
Arrange rapid testing of the source client after consent is obtained under facility policy
Postpone the evaluation until the employee's next scheduled shift
Enter the injury on the sharps injury log with the device type and the circumstances of the exposure
items.rationale: Exposure follow-up is time-critical because prophylaxis for human immunodeficiency virus works best within hours, so source testing, baseline serology and the decision about prophylaxis all happen the same day, followed by scheduled repeat testing and counseling. Logging the device and circumstances is a legal requirement and how the facility identifies the devices that cause injuries. The source client's identity and diagnosis remain confidential.

items.stem: A 9-year-old with epilepsy is enrolling at a school where rescue midazolam may be needed during the school day. Which action by the school nurse is required before that medication can be given at school?
options: Keep the medication in the school office and give it whenever a teacher reports that the student had a seizure
Give the medication to the student to carry so that it can be used whenever the student decides
Obtain a written provider order and written parental authorization, then train designated staff and document their competency in the student's individualized health plan
Ask a parent to come to the school and give the medication each time it is needed
items.rationale: Medication given at school requires both a current provider order stating the drug, dose, route and the specific criteria for giving it, and written parental authorization, and the plan works only if named staff are trained and their competency documented in the student's health plan. Acting on a teacher's report without those criteria is administering without an order. Relying on a parent delays a time-critical rescue medication, and a benzodiazepine is not a self-carry medication for a 9-year-old.
